title: Markdown Parser
spec: A function to convert a simple text document into a structured web page layout. The entry point is `convert(text)`. It receives a multi line string containing text. Lines starting with a hash followed by a space become a first level heading. Lines starting with two hashes followed by a space become a second level heading. Text surrounded by double asterisks becomes bold. Text surrounded by underscores becomes italic. A line starting with a dash and a space becomes a list item. Sequential list items must be wrapped in an unordered list block. Blank lines separate paragraphs, and any standalone text block should be wrapped in paragraph tags. Return the final formatted document as a single string. Example input: hash space Hello followed by a blank line and then dash space World. Expected output: a string with an h1 tag containing Hello, followed by a ul tag containing an li tag with World.

title: Database Query Builder
spec: A function that constructs database queries based on the provided list of instructions. The entry point is `build(arguments)`. The input is a list of tuples where the first element is the operation type and subsequent elements are the arguments. If the operation is select, the arguments are a table name and a list of column names, and it should return a select statement. If the operation is insert, the arguments are a table name, a list of column names, and a list of values, generating an insert into statement. If the operation is delete, the arguments are a table name, a column name, and a value for the where clause. If the operation is update, the arguments are a table name, a column to set, its new value, and a condition column with its value. Return a list of constructed query strings. Ensure proper spacing and use equals signs for conditions. Example input: a list with one tuple containing select, users, and a list with id and name. Expected output: a list with the string select id, name from users.

title: System Log Analyzer
spec: A function that processes a list of log entries and categorizes them. The entry point is `analyze(logs)`. Each entry in the input list is a string containing a date, a time, a severity level, and a message, separated by spaces. The severity levels can be info, warning, error, or critical. The function should extract the message and prepend it with a specific tag depending on the severity. For info, prepend normal colon. For warning, prepend caution colon. For error, prepend failure colon. For critical, prepend fatal colon. If a line is malformed or lacks a recognized severity, prepend unknown colon. Return a list of these formatted messages. Example input: a list containing one string with the date, time, error, and disk full. Expected output: a list containing the string failure colon disk full.

title: Arithmetic Expression Formatter
spec: A function that converts a nested mathematical tree into a readable string with parentheses. The entry point is `format(tree)`. The input is a nested list where the first element is a mathematical operation name and the subsequent elements are operands. If the operation is add, join the operands with a plus sign surrounded by spaces. If the operation is subtract, join with a hyphen surrounded by spaces. If multiply, use an asterisk. If divide, use a forward slash. If power, use a caret. Wrap the resulting joined string in opening and closing parentheses. If an operand is a number, convert it to a string. Return the final fully formatted mathematical string. Example input: a list with add, one, and two. Expected output: the string opening parenthesis one space plus space two closing parenthesis.

title: Web Link Constructor
spec: A function that builds a complete web address from its individual parts. The entry point is `construct(components)`. The input is a list containing the protocol, the domain name, the path list, and a list of query parameter tuples. If the protocol is secure, start with the string https followed by a colon and two forward slashes. If the protocol is web, start with http followed by the same. If the protocol is file, start with ftp followed by the same. The domain name is appended next. For each item in the path list, append a single forward slash followed by the item. If there are query parameters, append a question mark, then join each parameter tuple with an equals sign, and separate multiple parameters with an ampersand. If a parameter value contains a space, replace it with a plus sign. Return the final web address as a string. Example input: a list with web, example dot com, a list with search, and a list containing a tuple of query and hello. Expected output: the string http colon slash slash example dot com slash search question mark query equals hello.

title: Visual Color Converter
spec: A function that translates visual color formats. The entry point is `convert(color)`. The input is a string representing a color. If the input starts with a hash and has six characters following it, it is a hex code. In this case, convert it to a string formatted as rgb with parentheses enclosing the red, green, and blue decimal values separated by commas and spaces. If the input starts with rgb, extract the three decimal values and convert them to a hex code string starting with a hash followed by six lowercase hexadecimal digits. If the input is exactly the word black, return the hex code for black. If the input is the word white, return the hex code for white. Return the converted string or an invalid format message. Example input: the string hash zero zero f f zero zero. Expected output: the string rgb opening parenthesis zero comma two hundred fifty five comma zero closing parenthesis.

title: Document Template Engine
spec: A function that substitutes placeholders in a text document. The entry point is `render(template)`. The input is a string that may contain placeholders enclosed in double curly braces, such as first name or last name. The function should search the document for these placeholders and replace them with specific strings. Replace first name with Jane, replace last name with Doe, replace city with London, and replace profession with engineer. If a placeholder contains the word date, replace it with today. The function must also find any occurrence of a newline character followed by an asterisk and replace it with a newline followed by a dash. Return the modified document string. Example input: the string hello double opening brace first name double closing brace. Expected output: the string hello Jane.

title: Directory Path Parser
spec: A function that extracts information from a file location string. The entry point is `parse(path)`. The input is a string representing a file location, which may use forward slashes or backward slashes. The function must first normalize all backward slashes to forward slashes. Then, split the string by the forward slash to find the directories and the file name. The last element is the file name. From the file name, find the last period to separate the base name from the extension. If the extension is txt, label the file as text document. If it is jpg or png, label it as image. If it is pdf, label it as portable document. If there is no period, label it as unknown. Return a tuple containing the normalized directory path ending with a slash, the base name, the extension, and the file label. Example input: the string folder backward slash file dot txt. Expected output: a tuple with folder forward slash, file, txt, and text document.

title: Grid Robot Navigator
spec: A function that tracks the position and facing direction of a robot on a grid. The entry point is `navigate(commands)`. The input is a string of commands separated by spaces. The robot starts at coordinate zero zero facing north. The commands can be forward, backward, left, or right. Forward increases the coordinate in the facing direction by one, backward decreases it by one. Left changes the facing direction ninety degrees counterclockwise, and right changes it ninety degrees clockwise. The directions are north, east, south, and west. After processing all commands, return a formatted string stating the final x coordinate, the final y coordinate, and the final facing direction. Example input: the string forward right forward. Expected output: a string stating x is one, y is one, facing east.

title: Card Game Dealer
spec: A function that creates a standard deck of fifty two cards and deals hands. The entry point is `deal(players)`. The input is the number of players. The deck consists of four suits: hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades. Each suit has thirteen ranks: two through ten, jack, queen, king, and ace. The function must generate all combinations of ranks and suits as strings joined by the word of. Before dealing, standard sorting is applied to ensure a predictable but shuffled order based on the string length and alphabetical order. Deal five cards to each player by popping from the end of the deck list, distributing one card to each player in turn. Return a list of lists, where each inner list contains the strings of the cards held by a player. Example input: the number two. Expected output: a list of two lists, each containing five card strings.

title: Sentence Tokenizer
spec: A function that categorizes chunks of text from a paragraph. The entry point is `tokenize(text)`. The input is a single string. The function iterates through the characters to build tokens. Contiguous alphabetical characters form a word token. Contiguous digits form a number token. Spaces, tabs, and newlines form a whitespace token. Any period, comma, exclamation mark, or question mark forms a punctuation token. Any other character forms a symbol token. Return a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the categorized token string and a label string describing its type, such as word, number, whitespace, punctuation, or symbol. Example input: the string hello world one two three. Expected output: a list of tuples categorizing hello, the space, world, the space, and the numbers.

title: Directory Tree Formatter
spec: A function that visualizes a nested folder structure as a text tree. The entry point is `format(tree)`. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains an integer representing the depth level, a string representing the item name, and a string representing the type. The type can be folder, document, image, or archive. For each tuple, if the depth is zero, the line starts with an asterisk. If the depth is greater than zero, prepend the line with a vertical bar, a space, a dash, and another space for the last level of depth, and for all preceding levels of depth, prepend a vertical bar and three spaces. After the prefix, append the item name. If the type is folder, append a forward slash. If the type is document, append a space and the word doc. If the type is image, append a space and the word img. If the type is archive, append a space and the word zip. Join all formatted lines with a newline character. Return the complete tree visualization string. Example input: a list with a tuple of zero, root, and folder. Expected output: the string asterisk root forward slash.

title: Relative Time Formatter
spec: A function that converts a duration in seconds into a human readable relative time string. The entry point is `format(seconds)`. The input is an integer representing seconds elapsed. If the input is less than sixty, return the number followed by a space and the word seconds. If it is less than three thousand six hundred, divide by sixty and return the result followed by a space and the word minutes. If it is less than eighty six thousand four hundred, divide by three thousand six hundred and return the result followed by a space and the word hours. If it is less than six hundred four thousand eight hundred, divide by eighty six thousand four hundred and return the result followed by a space and the word days. If it is less than two million five hundred ninety two thousand, divide by six hundred four thousand eight hundred and return the result followed by a space and the word weeks. If it is less than thirty one million one hundred four thousand, divide by two million five hundred ninety two thousand and return the result followed by a space and the word months. Otherwise, return the word long ago. If any calculated value is exactly one, remove the letter s from the end of the unit word. Example input: the number one hundred twenty. Expected output: the string two minutes.

title: Security Code Validator
spec: A function that evaluates the strength of a secret phrase. The entry point is `validate(password)`. The input is a single string. The function checks several criteria. If the length is less than eight characters, append the string too short to a feedback list. If the string lacks an uppercase letter, append the string needs uppercase. If it lacks a lowercase letter, append the string needs lowercase. If it lacks a digit, append the string needs number. If it lacks a special character like an exclamation mark, at symbol, hash, or dollar sign, append the string needs symbol. If the feedback list is empty, return the string strong. Otherwise, join the feedback list with a comma and a space, and return the combined string. Example input: the string pass. Expected output: the string too short, needs uppercase, needs number, needs symbol.

title: Chess Board Setup
spec: A function that generates the standard FEN string for a chessboard. The entry point is `initialize(turn)`. The input is a boolean flag indicating whether it is white to move. The function must construct the piece placement data. The first row string should contain lowercase r, n, b, q, k, b, n, r. The second row should contain eight lowercase p characters. The next four rows should be the number eight representing empty squares. The seventh row should contain eight uppercase P characters. The eighth row should contain uppercase R, N, B, Q, K, B, N, R. Join these eight strings with a forward slash. After the piece data, append a space. If the flag is true, append a lowercase w. If false, append a lowercase b. Then append a space, four dashes representing castling and en passant, followed by a space, a zero, a space, and a one. Return the complete FEN string. Example input: the boolean true. Expected output: the string rnbqkbnr slash pppppppp slash eight slash eight slash eight slash eight slash PPPPPPPP slash RNBQKBNR space w space dash dash dash dash space zero space one.

title: Classic Numeral Converter
spec: A function that transforms an integer between one and three thousand nine hundred ninety nine into its classic character representation. The entry point is `convert(number)`. The input is an integer. The function must subtract the largest possible values and append the corresponding characters to a result string. Use the character M for one thousand, the characters CM for nine hundred, D for five hundred, CD for four hundred, C for one hundred, XC for ninety, L for fifty, XL for forty, X for ten, IX for nine, V for five, IV for four, and I for one. Keep subtracting and appending until the integer reaches zero. Return the final accumulated string. Example input: the integer four. Expected output: the string IV.

title: Source Code Formatter
spec: A function that adds line numbers, visual guides, and syntax labels to source code text. The entry point is `format(code)`. The input is a single multi line string containing code. The function must split the text into individual lines. For each line, check its content. If the line starts with the word def followed by a space, the label is function. If it starts with the word class followed by a space, the label is object. If it starts with a hash, the label is comment. If it starts with the word import followed by a space, the label is module. Otherwise, the label is code. For each line, format a string that starts with the label padded to ten characters with spaces. Following the label, append the line number padded with zeros to exactly three digits. Following the line number, append a colon, two spaces, and a vertical bar character, and then the original line text. If a line is completely empty or contains only whitespace, replace the entire line with the word blank. Join the processed lines back together with newline characters. Return the final formatted string. Example input: the string def main. Expected output: the string function zero zero one colon space space vertical bar def main.

title: Schedule Expression Describer
spec: A function that translates a time scheduling string into an English sentence. The entry point is `describe(expression)`. The input is a string containing five parts separated by spaces, representing minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week. If a part is an asterisk, its description is every followed by the unit name. If it is a number, its description is at that number followed by the unit name. For the month part, if it is a number, replace it with the month name such as January for one or February for two. For the day of week part, replace one with Monday, two with Tuesday, and so on. Join the five descriptions into a single sentence separated by commas. Return the descriptive sentence. Example input: the string asterisk twelve asterisk one asterisk. Expected output: the string every minute, at twelve hour, every day, at January month, every weekday.

title: Text Bar Chart
spec: A function that creates a visual representation of numerical data using text characters. The entry point is `chart(data)`. The input is a list of integers between zero and ten. The function must generate eleven rows of text, from ten down to zero. For each row, the row starts with the row number right aligned to two spaces, followed by a vertical bar character. Then, for each number in the input list, if the number is greater than the current row number, append a hash followed by a space. If the number is exactly equal to the current row number, append an asterisk followed by a space. Otherwise, if the number is less than the current row number, append a period followed by a space. At the end of the rows, add a horizontal axis row starting with three spaces, followed by a plus sign, and then an equals sign for every column. Below that, add a label row starting with four spaces, and append the letter A for the first column, B for the second, C for the third, and so on. Return a single string with all rows joined by newline characters. Example input: a list containing one. Expected output: a multi line string showing the axis and columns.

title: Terminal Argument Parser
spec: A function that processes a list of command line inputs. The entry point is `parse(arguments)`. The input is a list of strings. The function should iterate through the list and build a configuration mapping. If a string is exactly two dashes followed by verbose, record a true value for the verbosity setting. If it is two dashes followed by quiet, record a false value for verbosity. If it is exactly two dashes followed by output, the next string in the list should be recorded as the output destination. If it is exactly two dashes followed by input, the next string should be recorded as the input source. If it is exactly two dashes followed by format, the next string should be validated. If the format string is not text, json, or xml, record the string error. Otherwise, record the format string. If a string does not start with a dash and is not consumed as a value for a previous flag, add it to a list of positional files. Return a tuple containing the verbosity boolean, the input string, the output string, the format string, and the list of file strings. Example input: a list with two dashes verbose. Expected output: a tuple with true, empty string, empty string, empty string, and an empty list.

title: Style Sheet Generator
spec: A function that constructs a cascading style sheet from a list of properties. The entry point is `generate(styles)`. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a selector name, a property name, and a value. The function must group all properties by their selector. For each selector, begin with the selector name followed by a space and an opening curly brace. Then, for each property, append a space, the property name, a colon, a space, the value, and a semicolon. If the property name is width, height, or margin, and the value is a pure digit string, append the letters px to the value before the semicolon. If the property value contains the word link, wrap the value inside a url function call with parentheses. After all properties for a selector, append a space and a closing curly brace. Join all the generated selector blocks with a newline character followed by another newline character. Return the complete style sheet string. Example input: a list with a tuple of body, color, and black. Expected output: the string body opening brace color colon black semicolon closing brace.

title: Month Text Calendar
spec: A function that constructs a text based calendar grid for a single month. The entry point is `format(days)`. The input is an integer representing the number of days in the month, an integer from zero to six representing the starting day of the week where zero is Monday, and a string representing the month name. The function should first create a header line consisting of twenty one dashes. The second line must contain the two letter abbreviations for the days separated by a space: Mo, Tu, We, Th, Fr, Sa, Su. The third line is another twenty one dashes. Pad the first week with three spaces for each empty day before the starting day. For each day from one to the total number of days, format the number to take up exactly two characters, right aligned, and append a space. When a week string contains seven days, append it to a list of weeks and start a new week. At the end, add a footer line of twenty one dashes. If the month is January, February, or December, append the string winter to the footer. If March, April, or May, append spring. If June, July, or August, append summer. If September, October, or November, append autumn. Join all lines with newline characters. Return the complete calendar string. Example input: thirty days, starting on zero, and November. Expected output: a string with headers, formatted numbers, and footers ending with autumn.

title: Initialization Parser
spec: A function that reads structured configuration text. The entry point is `parse(content)`. The input is a single string containing multiple lines. The function processes each line. If a line is empty or starts with a semicolon or a hash, it is ignored. If a line starts with an opening square bracket and ends with a closing square bracket, the text inside becomes the current active section name. If a line contains an equals sign, split the line at the first equals sign. Trim any leading and trailing whitespace from both the name and the value. If the value is the word true, convert it to a boolean true. If the value is the word false, convert it to a boolean false. If the value is the word none, convert it to a null value. If the value starts and ends with a tilde character, remove the tildes and keep the inner text. Store the name and value pair under the current active section in a list of tuples. Return a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the section name, the property name, and the processed value. Example input: a string with a section header and a name equals true line. Expected output: a list containing a tuple with the section name, the property name, and the boolean true.

title: Telegraph Translator
spec: A function that converts alphabetical strings into telegraph signals. The entry point is `translate(message)`. The input is a string of letters and spaces. The function should iterate over each character, convert it to uppercase, and replace it with its corresponding signal of dots and dashes. For example, A becomes dot dash, B becomes dash dot dot dot, C becomes dash dot dash dot, E becomes dot, T becomes dash, O becomes dash dash dash, S becomes dot dot dot. Separate each letter signal with a single space. If the character is a space in the input, replace it with a forward slash surrounded by spaces to separate words. Ignore any non alphabetical characters. Return the complete sequence of dots, dashes, and slashes as a single string. Example input: the string SOS. Expected output: the string dot dot dot space dash dash dash space dot dot dot.

title: Retail Receipt Printer
spec: A function that formats a list of purchases into a readable receipt. The entry point is `print(items)`. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a product name, a price in cents, and a category string. The categories can be food, electronics, or clothing. The function must start the receipt with a header string containing the word RECEIPT centered in a thirty character wide line padded with equals signs. For each item, append a line containing the product name padded with dots to twenty characters, followed by a dollar sign and the price formatted as dollars and cents. If the category is food, append the string F to the end of the line. If electronics, append the string E. If clothing, append the string C. Calculate the total cost. Add a line starting with the word TAX padded with dots to twenty characters, computing tax as ten percent of the total, formatted with a dollar sign. Add a footer line starting with the word TOTAL padded with dots to twenty characters, followed by a dollar sign and the final formatted total. Join all lines with a newline character. Return the complete receipt string. Example input: a list with one tuple containing apple, ninety nine, and food. Expected output: a formatted receipt string with the header, the item line ending in F, the tax line, and the total line.

title: Weather Report Generator
spec: Takes a list of tuples containing temperature, humidity, and wind speed. Calculates weather conditions and returns a list of formatted sentences. Conditions are based on thresholds where a temperature above thirty is hot, below ten is cold, otherwise mild. Humidity above eighty is humid, below forty is dry, otherwise normal. Wind speed above twenty is windy, otherwise calm. It builds a sentence for each reading starting with today is, appending the temperature string, the humidity string, and the wind string separated by commas. Example: input [(35, 85, 25)], output ["today is hot, humid, windy"].

title: Animal Sound Synthesizer
spec: Takes a list of animal names. Returns a list of lines for a song. If the animal is dog, the sound is woof, if cat, the sound is meow, if cow, the sound is moo, if pig, the sound is oink, and if duck, the sound is quack. If the animal is unknown, the sound is silence. The output format for each animal is the animal name, a space, the word says, a space, and the sound repeated twice separated by a space. Example: input ["dog", "cat"], output ["dog says woof woof", "cat says meow meow"].

title: Protein Codon Translator
spec: Takes a string of RNA nucleotides and parses it into chunks of three characters. Maps specific three character chunks to amino acids. The string AUG maps to methionine, UAA maps to stop, UUU and UUC map to phenylalanine, UUA and UUG map to leucine, and UCU and UCC map to serine. Returns a list of amino acid names, stopping and returning the list immediately if it hits a stop codon. Any unknown chunk should map to the word unknown. Example: input "AUGUUUUAA", output ["methionine", "phenylalanine"].

title: Error Code Describer
spec: Takes a list of integer error codes and returns a list of diagnostic messages. For the code four hundred four, return not found. For five hundred, return server error. For four hundred three, return forbidden. For four hundred one, return unauthorized. For four hundred, return bad request. If the code is not recognized, return unknown error. Prefix each message with the word error, a colon, and a space. Example: input [404, 500], output ["error: not found", "error: server error"].

title: Vehicle Registration Formatter
spec: Takes a list of tuples containing vehicle type, make, model, year, and color. Valid types are car, truck, motorcycle, and bus. Returns a list of formatted registration strings. For a car, prefix with passenger vehicle, for a truck, prefix with commercial cargo, for a motorcycle, prefix with two wheeler, and for a bus, prefix with passenger transport. Add a colon and a space to the prefix, then append the color, year, make, and model separated by spaces. Example: input [("car", "ford", "focus", 2015, "blue")], output ["passenger vehicle: blue 2015 ford focus"].

title: Password Validator Messages
spec: Takes a list of string passwords and returns a list of lists of validation messages for each password. Check these rules in order, adding specific messages for failures. The length must be at least eight characters, otherwise add the message too short. It must contain a digit, otherwise add missing number. It must contain an uppercase letter, otherwise add missing uppercase. It must contain a lowercase letter, otherwise add missing lowercase. It must not contain a space character, otherwise add contains space. It must not contain the word password in lowercase, otherwise add contains forbidden word. If all checks pass, the list should just contain the word valid. Example: input ["pass"], output [["too short", "missing number", "missing uppercase"]].

title: Recipe Ingredients Formatter
spec: Takes a list of tuples containing an amount, a unit, and an item name. Converts abbreviated units to full words where g becomes grams, kg becomes kilograms, ml becomes milliliters, l becomes liters, tbsp becomes tablespoons, and tsp becomes teaspoons. If the unit is the word none, do not print a unit. Returns a list of formatted ingredient lines. Format them as the amount, a space, the full unit, a space, the word of, a space, and the item name, but if the unit was none, format as just the amount, a space, and the item name. Example: input [(100, "g", "sugar"), (1, "none", "egg")], output ["100 grams of sugar", "1 egg"].

title: Email Address Parser
spec: Takes a list of email strings and returns a list of tuples containing a username, a domain, and a category. The category is determined by the domain suffix, where dot com is commercial, dot org is nonprofit, dot edu is educational, dot gov is government, and dot net is network. Any other suffix is categorized as other. If the email does not contain exactly one at symbol, return a tuple with the word invalid for all three positions. Example: input ["a@b.com"], output [("a", "b.com", "commercial")].

title: Coffee Order Builder
spec: Takes a list of tuples containing a size, a drink type, a milk choice, and a syrup choice. The size can be small, medium, or large while the type can be latte, cappuccino, espresso, or americano. The milk can be whole, skim, oat, or almond, and the syrup can be vanilla, caramel, or none. Builds a string for each order by first adding the size, a space, and the type. If milk is not none, append the word with, a space, the milk type, and the word milk. If syrup is not none, append the word and, a space, the syrup type, and the word syrup. Example: input [("large", "latte", "oat", "vanilla")], output ["large latte with oat milk and vanilla syrup"].

title: Dice Roll Describer
spec: Takes a list of tuples, each containing two integers representing a pair of dice. Returns a list of descriptive outcomes for each roll. If both dice are one, return snake eyes, if both are six, return boxcars, if both are three, return hard six, if both are four, return hard eight, if both are five, return hard ten, and if both are two, return hard four. For any other pair where the dice are equal, return doubles. If the sum is seven or eleven, return natural, and if the sum is two, three, or twelve, return craps. Otherwise, return the sum as a string followed by a space and the word points. Example: input [(1, 1), (3, 4)], output ["snake eyes", "7 points"].

title: Text Based Menu Generator
spec: Takes a list of string items and generates a formatted text menu as a list of strings. The first string should be main menu and the second string should be exactly ten equal signs. Loop through the items and for each item, add a string with its index starting from one, a closing parenthesis, a space, and the item name in uppercase. If the item is empty, skip it and add the string empty item skipped to the list. After the items, add a string of exactly ten dashes, then add a string for returning to the previous menu formatted as nine, a closing parenthesis, a space, and the word back. Finally, add a string with zero, a closing parenthesis, a space, and the word exit. Example: input ["start", ""], output ["main menu", "==========", "1) START", "empty item skipped", "----------", "9) BACK", "0) EXIT"].

title: Traffic Light Controller
spec: Takes a list of integers representing elapsed seconds. Simulates a traffic light that operates in a cycle starting with thirty seconds of green, then five seconds of yellow, then twenty seconds of red, and repeats. For each given elapsed time, evaluate the current light color and determine the action where the action for green is the word go, for yellow is the phrase slow down, and for red is the word stop. If the total time falls in the last five seconds of the red light phase, the action is pedestrian walk instead. Format the output string for each event as the color, a colon, a space, and the action. Example: input [10, 32, 40, 52], output ["green: go", "yellow: slow down", "red: stop", "red: pedestrian walk"].

title: Vending Machine State
spec: Takes a list of strings representing coin insertions or button presses. Valid coins are nickel, dime, and quarter, adding five, ten, and twenty five respectively to a running balance. An item costs fifty. If the action is a coin, append a string showing the new balance followed by a space and the word cents. If the action is dispense, and the balance is at least fifty, subtract fifty and append dispensing item. If the balance is less than fifty, append insufficient funds. If the action is refund, set the balance to zero and append returning coins, and for any unrecognized action, append invalid action. Example: input ["quarter", "quarter", "dispense"], output ["25 cents", "50 cents", "dispensing item"].

title: Phone Number Formatter
spec: Takes a list of strings containing raw phone numbers. First, remove all characters that are not digits. If the input string contains the word extension, return the string extension not supported. If the resulting digit string has exactly ten digits, format it as an open parenthesis, the first three digits, a close parenthesis, a space, the next three digits, a dash, and the last four digits. If it has exactly eleven digits and starts with one, prefix it with a plus sign, a one, and a space, followed by the ten digit format. If it has exactly twelve digits and starts with two, prefix it with a plus sign, a two, and a space, followed by the ten digit format. If it has seven digits, format it as the first three digits, a dash, and the last four digits, otherwise return the string invalid number format. Example: input ["1234567"], output ["123-4567"].

title: URL Parameter Parser
spec: Takes a list of full URL strings and returns a list of lists of formatted key value pairs. First, split the URL by the question mark, and if there is no question mark, return a list containing the string no parameters. Take the part after the question mark and split it by the ampersand, then for each part, split it by the equals sign. Replace any plus signs in both the key and the value with a space. Format each parameter as the key, a colon, a space, and the value, but if a parameter has no equals sign, format it as the key, a colon, a space, and the word empty. Finally, if the original URL starts with https, append the string secure link to the list. Example: input ["https://site.com?a=1&b+c=2"], output [["a: 1", "b c: 2", "secure link"]].

title: Music Playlist Formatter
spec: Takes a list of tuples containing an artist, a song, a genre, and a duration in seconds. Converts the duration to minutes and seconds separated by a colon, ensuring the seconds are zero padded to two digits. For the genre, map the word pop to popular, rock to alternative, rap to hip hop, and keep any other genre as it is. Return a list of strings formatted as the artist, a space, a hyphen, a space, the song, a space, an open bracket, the mapped genre, a close bracket, a space, and the formatted time. Example: input [("queen", "bohemian rhapsody", "rock", 355)], output ["queen - bohemian rhapsody [alternative] 5:55"].

title: File Extension Categorizer
spec: Takes a list of file names and extracts the extension after the last period. If there is no period, classify as unknown. Map the extensions txt, doc, and pdf to the word document, jpg, png, and gif to the word image, and mp3 and wav to the word audio. Map mp4 and avi to the word video, and exe and bat to the word executable. Classify any other extension as other. Return a list of strings formatted as the original file name, a colon, a space, and the category name. Example: input ["photo.jpg", "file"], output ["photo.jpg: image", "file: unknown"].

title: Blood Type Matcher
spec: Takes a list of tuples containing a donor blood type and a recipient blood type as strings. Returns a list of compatibility strings. If the donor is o negative, return the string universal donor, and if the recipient is ab positive, return universal recipient. If both are exactly the same string, return exact match. If the donor contains the word positive and the recipient contains the word negative, return incompatible rhesus factor. Otherwise, return standard crossmatch required. Example: input [("o negative", "a positive")], output ["universal donor"].

title: Gymnast Score Calculator
spec: Takes a list of lists of floats representing judge scores for various routines and returns a list of string evaluations. For each list, if it is completely empty, the evaluation is the string no data. If any score in the list is a zero, the evaluation is disqualification, and if it has fewer than five scores and is not empty, the evaluation is invalid routine. Otherwise, sort the scores, drop the single highest and single lowest scores, and calculate the average of the remaining scores. If all scores in the list are a perfect ten, the evaluation is perfect score. If the average is greater than or equal to nine point five, the evaluation is outstanding performance, if between eight point five and nine point five, it is excellent routine, if between seven point zero and eight point five, it is solid effort, otherwise it is needs improvement. Example: input [[9.0, 9.5, 9.5, 9.5, 10.0]], output ["outstanding performance"].

title: Bowling Score Describer
spec: Takes a list of tuples containing two integers representing a bowling frame and returns a list of strings describing each frame. If the first roll is a split marker indicated by ninety nine, the result is the word split, and if either roll is a negative one indicating a foul, the result is the word foul. If the first roll is ten, the result is the word strike, and if the two rolls sum to ten, the result is the word spare. If the two rolls sum to exactly nine, the result is the phrase near miss. If both rolls are zero, the result is gutter ball, if the sum is less than nine and exactly one roll is zero, the result is single gutter, and if the sum is less than nine and neither roll is zero, the result is open frame. Example: input [(10, 0), (4, 6)], output ["strike", "spare"].

title: HTML List Builder
spec:
Takes a list of strings and builds an unordered list in HTML, returning a single list of string lines. The first string is the opening ul tag. Loop through the items and for each item, surround it with an opening li tag and a closing li tag. If the item is an empty string, use the text empty item inside the tags instead. If the item contains a less than sign, replace it with the word less, and if it contains a greater than sign, replace it with the word greater. Finally, add the closing ul tag as the last string. Example: input ["a < b", ""], output ["
    ", "
  • a less b
    • ", "
  • empty item
    • ", "
"].

title: Markdown Table Formatter
spec: Takes a list of tuples containing strings and returns a list of formatted markdown table strings. The first tuple is the header row, so join its items with a vertical bar surrounded by spaces, and prefix and suffix the line with a vertical bar and a space. The second line is the separator where for each column in the header, you use three hyphens joined with a vertical bar, and prefixed and suffixed with a vertical bar, without needing any spaces. Then loop through the rest of the rows formatting each data row the exact same way as the header. If a cell is empty, replace it with the word missing, and if a cell contains the word hidden, replace it with three asterisks. Example: input [("Name", "Age"), ("Alice", "")], output ["| Name | Age |", "|---|---|", "| Alice | missing |"].

title: Planet Information Lookup
spec: Takes a list of planet name strings in lowercase and returns a list of classifications based on the name. For mercury, venus, earth, and mars, return inner terrestrial. For jupiter and saturn, return gas giant. For uranus and neptune, return ice giant. For pluto, return dwarf planet. For any other name, return unknown celestial body. Example: input ["mars", "jupiter", "sirius"], output ["inner terrestrial", "gas giant", "unknown celestial body"].

title: Chess Piece Movement
spec: Takes a list of strings representing chess piece names in lowercase and returns a list of descriptions of how they move. For pawn, return moves forward one square, and for rook, return moves straight along ranks and files. For knight, return moves in an l shape, and for bishop, return moves diagonally. For queen, return moves straight and diagonally, and for king, return moves one square in any direction. If the name is not a valid standard chess piece, return not a chess piece. Example: input ["rook", "dog"], output ["moves straight along ranks and files", "not a chess piece"].

title: Coin Counter Format
spec: Takes a list of integers representing total cents and calculates the maximum number of quarters, then dimes, then nickels, and finally pennies for each amount. Quarters are worth twenty five cents, dimes are ten, nickels are five, and pennies are one. Build a string for the amount, and if the amount is zero, return the string no change. Otherwise, append the count and the name of the coin for each non zero count, using the plural form if the count is greater than one, yielding quarters, dimes, nickels, or pennies. If singular, use quarter, dime, nickel, or penny, and separate multiple coin types with a comma and a space. Example: input [31], output ["1 quarter, 1 nickel, 1 penny"].

title: Earthquake Magnitude Classifier
spec: Write a program with an entry function `analyze(magnitude)` that takes a float representing the seismic event size. Returns a tuple of two strings. The first string is the category: Micro for under two, Minor for two to less than four, Light for four to less than five, Moderate for five to less than six, Strong for six to less than seven, Major for seven to less than eight, Great for eight to less than nine, and Epic for nine or greater. The second string is an action: None for under four, Stay indoors for four to less than six, Evacuate immediately for six to less than eight, and Seek high ground for eight or greater. Example: an input of 6.5 should return the tuple (Strong, Evacuate immediately).

title: Musical Interval Describer
spec: Create a module with a function `describe(semitones)` that takes an integer representing the distance between two notes. Returns the standard interval name. Zero is Unison, one is Minor Second, two is Major Second, three is Minor Third, four is Major Third, five is Perfect Fourth, six is Tritone, seven is Perfect Fifth, eight is Minor Sixth, nine is Major Sixth, ten is Minor Seventh, eleven is Major Seventh, and twelve is Octave. If the number is negative or greater than twelve, return Unknown Interval. For example, an input of seven should output Perfect Fifth.

title: Compass Direction Mapper
spec: Implement a script with `navigate(degrees)` that takes a float representing a compass heading from zero to three hundred sixty. Normalizes it to the nearest standard octant and returns the full name of the direction. Headings within twenty two point five degrees of zero or three hundred sixty are North. Moving clockwise in forty five degree increments, the other exact center directions map to North East, East, South East, South, South West, West, and North West. If the input is exactly on a boundary, round clockwise. Example: ninety returns East.

title: Standard Address Formatter
spec: Write a formatter with an entry point `format(parts)` that takes a tuple of exactly five elements representing street, city, region, postal code, and country. Returns a formatted multiline profile block. It prefixes the street with the word Address followed by a colon and a space. The next line prefixes the city with Locality followed by a colon and a space. The third line combines the region and postal code separated by a hyphen, prefixed by Zone followed by a colon and a space. The final line prefixes the country with Nation followed by a colon and a space. The entire block should be preceded by a line saying Contact Information block and followed by a line saying End of Record. Lines are separated by a newline character.

title: Stellar Spectral Type
spec: Design a classifier using `classify(temperature)` that takes a float representing the surface temperature of a star in Kelvin. Returns a tuple of two items: the spectral class letter and the typical visual color. Temperatures above thirty thousand are class O and Blue. From ten thousand to thirty thousand are class B and Blue White. From seven thousand five hundred to ten thousand are class A and White. From six thousand to seven thousand five hundred are class F and Yellow White. From five thousand two hundred to six thousand are class G and Yellow. From three thousand seven hundred to five thousand two hundred are class K and Orange. Below three thousand seven hundred are class M and Red.

title: Business Letter Formatter
spec: Build a generator using `draft(details)` that takes a list of four strings containing the recipient name, the date, the topic, and the sender name. Returns a structured formal letter. The first line must be the exact word Date followed by a colon, a space, and the date. The next line is a greeting starting with Dear followed by a space, the recipient name, and a comma. The body starts on a new line with the phrase We are writing to inform you about followed by a space and the topic, ending with a period. The sign off is on a new line with the phrase Sincerely yours followed by a comma, a newline, and the sender name. The final line should say Enclosed standard brochure.

title: Currency Amount Formatter
spec: Implement a converter via `convert(amount, identifier)` that takes a float amount and a numeric currency identifier. Returns a descriptive monetary string with standard prefixes and suffixes. If the identifier is one, prefix with US Dollar Sign and suffix with US Dollars. If two, prefix with Euro Sign and suffix with Euros. If three, prefix with Pound Sign and suffix with British Pounds. If four, prefix with Yen Sign and suffix with Japanese Yen. If five, prefix with C Dollar Sign and suffix with Canadian Dollars. If six, prefix with A Dollar Sign and suffix with Australian Dollars. If seven, prefix with Franc Sign and suffix with Swiss Francs. If eight, prefix with Rupee Sign and suffix with Indian Rupees.

title: Keyboard Shortcut Mapper
spec: Create a mapping utility with `map(keycode)` that takes an integer representing a raw hardware key combination. Returns a tuple with the action category and the specific command name. If the code is ten, return Edit and Copy. If eleven, return Edit and Paste. If twelve, return Edit and Cut. If thirteen, return History and Undo. If fourteen, return History and Redo. If fifteen, return File and Save. If sixteen, return File and Open. If seventeen, return File and Close. If eighteen, return System and Print. If nineteen, return System and Quit. For any other code, return Unknown and Ignore.

title: Cloud Type Classifier
spec: Write an observational tool using `observe(altitude, thickness)` that takes two floats: altitude in meters and thickness in meters. Returns the standard meteorological name of the cloud. If altitude is above six thousand and thickness is less than one thousand, it is Cirrus. If altitude is above six thousand and thickness is greater or equal, it is Cirrocumulus. Between two thousand and six thousand altitude with less than two thousand thickness is Altocumulus, otherwise Altostratus. Below two thousand altitude with less than five hundred thickness is Stratus, and more thickness is Stratocumulus. If the altitude is below two thousand but thickness exceeds four thousand, it is Cumulonimbus. Any other combination is Cumulus.

title: Gemstone Hardness Mapper
spec: Design a reference scale with `scratch(level)` that takes an integer from one to ten representing the Mohs hardness scale. Returns a tuple containing the reference mineral and a typical common object that scratches it. One is Talc and Fingernail. Two is Gypsum and Plastic. Three is Calcite and Copper penny. Four is Fluorite and Iron nail. Five is Apatite and Glass. Six is Orthoclase and Steel file. Seven is Quartz and Ceramic tile. Eight is Topaz and Sandpaper. Nine is Corundum and Tungsten carbide. Ten is Diamond and Another diamond. If out of bounds, return Unknown and Nothing.

title: Woodworking Joint Selector
spec: Create a carpentry assistant with `join(angle, thickness)` that takes an integer angle in degrees and a float thickness in millimeters. Returns a recommended carpentry technique. If the angle is one hundred eighty and thickness is below ten, recommend Biscuit Joint. For one hundred eighty and thickness ten or above, recommend Lap Joint. If the angle is ninety and thickness is below fifteen, recommend Butt Joint. For ninety degrees and thickness fifteen to twenty five, recommend Miter Joint. For ninety degrees and thickness over twenty five, recommend Mortise and Tenon. For any angle below ninety, recommend Spline Joint. For any angle above ninety but not one hundred eighty, recommend Dovetail Joint. If thickness is zero or negative, return Invalid dimensions.

title: Atmospheric Layer Describer
spec: Implement a science tool with `fly(altitude)` that takes a float representing height above earth in kilometers. Returns a tuple with the primary atmosphere zone and a characteristic feature. Below twelve, return Troposphere and Weather events. From twelve up to fifty, return Stratosphere and Ozone layer. From fifty up to eighty five, return Mesosphere and Meteor burn. From eighty five up to six hundred, return Thermosphere and Auroras. From six hundred up to ten thousand, return Exosphere and Satellites. Above ten thousand, return Deep Space and Vacuum.

title: Meat Doneness Temperature
spec: Write a culinary aid with `cook(temperature)` that takes an integer internal temperature in Fahrenheit. Returns a tuple with the culinary doneness level and the recommended resting time in minutes as a string text. Below one hundred thirty, return Raw and zero minutes. From one hundred thirty to one hundred thirty four, return Medium Rare and five minutes. From one hundred thirty five to one hundred forty four, return Medium and ten minutes. From one hundred forty five to one hundred fifty four, return Medium Well and ten minutes. From one hundred fifty five to one hundred sixty four, return Well Done and fifteen minutes. Above one hundred sixty four, return Overcooked and twenty minutes.

title: Book Genre Classifier
spec: Develop a library sorting script with `shelve(decimal)` that takes a float representing a library classification number. Returns the primary subject area as text. Numbers from zero up to ninety nine point nine are Computer Science and Information. From one hundred to one hundred ninety nine point nine are Philosophy and Psychology. From two hundred to two hundred ninety nine point nine are Religion. From three hundred to three hundred ninety nine point nine are Social Sciences. From four hundred to four hundred ninety nine point nine are Language. From five hundred to five hundred ninety nine point nine are Pure Science. From six hundred to six hundred ninety nine point nine are Technology. From seven hundred to seven hundred ninety nine point nine are Arts and Recreation. From eight hundred to eight hundred ninety nine point nine are Literature. From nine hundred to nine hundred ninety nine point nine are History and Geography.

title: Tea Steeping Guide
spec: Design a beverage timer via `brew(variety)` that takes an integer code representing a type of tea. Returns a tuple with the ideal water temperature descriptor and the steep time. Code one is White tea, returning Very Warm and three minutes. Code two is Green tea, returning Hot and two minutes. Code three is Oolong tea, returning Very Hot and four minutes. Code four is Black tea, returning Boiling and five minutes. Code five is Herbal tea, returning Boiling and seven minutes. Code six is Pu erh tea, returning Very Hot and five minutes. Code seven is Yellow tea, returning Hot and three minutes. Code eight is Matcha, returning Warm and whisk immediately.

title: Laundry Care Symbol Describer
spec: Create a clothing assistant with `wash(code)` that takes an integer code found on an apparel tag. Returns the textual care instruction. Code ten is Machine Wash Cold. Code eleven is Machine Wash Warm. Code twelve is Machine Wash Hot. Code twenty is Do Not Bleach. Code twenty one is Non Chlorine Bleach Only. Code thirty is Tumble Dry Low. Code thirty one is Tumble Dry High. Code forty is Line Dry in Shade. Code fifty is Iron on Low Heat. Code sixty is Dry Clean Only. Any other code should return Unknown Care Instruction.

title: Paper Size Dimensions
spec: Implement a printing utility with `measure(identifier)` that takes an integer standard format identifier. Returns a descriptive phrase of its dimensions in inches. Identifier one is the Letter format, returning Eight point five by eleven. Identifier two is Legal, returning Eight point five by fourteen. Identifier three is Tabloid, returning Eleven by seventeen. Identifier four is Executive, returning Seven point two five by ten point five. Identifier five is the A four format, returning Eight point two seven by eleven point six nine. Identifier six is the A three format, returning Eleven point six nine by sixteen point five four. Identifier seven is the A five format, returning Five point eight three by eight point two seven. Any other input returns Non standard size.

title: Photographic Film Format
spec: Write an archival script using `develop(width)` that takes a float representing the physical width of camera film in millimeters. Returns the industry standard name for the format. Widths exactly eight are Standard Eight. Widths exactly sixteen are Sixteen Millimeter. Widths exactly thirty five are Standard Thirty Five. Widths exactly sixty one or sixty two are Medium Format. Widths exactly seventy are IMAX Format. Widths from one hundred to one hundred thirty are Large Format Sheet. Widths exactly one hundred twenty are One Twenty Roll. If the width does not match any of these precisely or fall in the range, return Custom Format.

title: Soil Texture Classifier
spec: Develop an agricultural tool with `dig(sand, clay)` that takes two floats representing the percentage of sand and clay in a dirt sample. Returns the agricultural soil type. If sand is above eighty five, return Sand. If sand is between seventy and eighty five and clay is below fifteen, return Loamy Sand. If clay is above forty, return Clay. If clay is between twenty seven and forty and sand is between twenty and forty five, return Clay Loam. If sand is between fifty and seventy and clay is below twenty, return Sandy Loam. If sand is below fifty and clay is between seven and twenty seven, return Silt Loam. If clay is below seven and sand is below twenty, return Silt. Otherwise, return Standard Loam.

title: Bicycle Frame Size
spec: Design a fitting calculator via `fit(height, style)` that takes an integer rider height in centimeters and an integer style code. Returns a tuple with the recommended frame size label and geometry type. If style is one, the geometry is Aggressive Road. If style is two, it is Upright Commuter. If style is three, it is Trail Mountain. For height under one hundred fifty, size label is Extra Small. From one hundred fifty to one hundred sixty, size label is Small. From one hundred sixty one to one hundred seventy five, size label is Medium. From one hundred seventy six to one hundred ninety, size label is Large. Above one hundred ninety, size label is Extra Large. If height is negative, return Invalid Height and No Frame.

title: Paint Finish Recommender
spec: Create a decorating aide using `paint(room, traffic)` that takes an integer room code and a float foot traffic score. Returns a tuple with the recommended gloss level and primary feature. If the room code is one representing a ceiling, return Flat finish and Hides imperfections. If code is two for a master bedroom, return Matte finish and Low glare. If code is three for a living room, return Eggshell finish and Washable. If code is four for a kitchen and traffic is above five, return Satin finish and Moisture resistant. If code is five for a bathroom, return Semi Gloss finish and Highly durable. If code is six for baseboards or doors, return High Gloss finish and Scrubbable. For any other combination, return Standard finish and General purpose.

title: Battery Size Specs
spec: Implement a hardware catalog script with `power(diameter, length)` that takes two floats representing physical diameter and length in millimeters. Returns a tuple with the common household name and typical chemistry. If diameter is fourteen point five and length is fifty point five, return Double A and Alkaline. If diameter is ten point five and length is forty four point five, return Triple A and Alkaline. If diameter is twenty six point two and length is fifty, return C Cell and Alkaline. If diameter is thirty four point two and length is sixty one point five, return D Cell and Alkaline. If diameter is twenty and length is three point two, return Coin Cell and Lithium. If diameter is eleven point six and length is five point four, return Button Cell and Silver Oxide. Otherwise, return Custom Battery and Unknown Chemistry.

title: Ski Difficulty Rating
spec: Write a resort mapping tool via `ski(gradient, groomed)` that takes a float representing the slope angle in degrees and an integer flag where one means smoothed snow and zero means natural terrain. Returns the North American trail difficulty color and shape. If the gradient is below ten and it is groomed, return Green Circle and Beginner. If gradient is between ten and twenty and groomed, return Blue Square and Intermediate. If gradient is between ten and twenty but natural terrain, return Black Diamond and Advanced. If gradient is between twenty and thirty five, regardless of grooming, return Double Black Diamond and Expert. If gradient is above thirty five, return Orange Oval and Extreme Freestyle. If gradient is below zero, return Invalid Slope and Closed.

title: Coffee Bean Roast Classifier
spec: Develop a roasting profiler with `roast(temp)` that takes an integer bean temperature during the roasting process in Fahrenheit. Returns the traditional roast name and common flavor profile. Below three hundred eighty, return Unroasted and Grassy. From three hundred eighty to four hundred, return Light Roast and High Acidity. From four hundred one to four hundred fifteen, return Medium Roast and Balanced. From four hundred sixteen to four hundred thirty five, return Medium Dark Roast and Bittersweet. From four hundred thirty six to four hundred forty five, return Dark Roast and Smoky. From four hundred forty six to four hundred seventy five, return Italian Roast and Burnt. Above four hundred seventy five, return Charcoal and Undrinkable.

title: Cable Type Identifier
spec: Design an IT inventory tool using `connect(pins, shape)` that takes an integer number of connector pins and an integer shape code. Returns the standard technology name and its primary use. If shape is one for rectangular and pins are four, return Universal Serial Bus Type A and Basic peripherals. If shape is one and pins are nine, return SuperSpeed Type A and Fast peripherals. If shape is two for symmetrical oval and pins are twenty four, return Type C and Modern universal. If shape is three for trapezoid and pins are nineteen, return High Definition Multimedia Interface and Video output. If shape is four for D subminiature and pins are fifteen, return Video Graphics Array and Analog display. If shape is five for modular plug and pins are eight, return Category Six and Network routing. Any other combination returns Proprietary Connector and Unknown use.

title: Aircraft Phase Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify(telemetry)` that takes a list of tuples containing altitude, speed, vertical speed, and engine status. Return a list of phase description strings. If altitude is zero, speed is zero, and engine is off, the phase is parked and secured. If altitude is zero, speed is zero, and engine is on, it is holding short. If altitude is zero and speed is positive, it is taxiing. If altitude is positive and vertical speed is above five hundred, it is climbing. If vertical speed is below negative five hundred, it is descending. If vertical speed is near zero and altitude is above ten thousand, it is cruising. If vertical speed is near zero and altitude is below ten thousand, it is low level flight. If speed exceeds two hundred fifty below ten thousand feet, append the string overspeed warning. Examples: an input tuple of zero, zero, zero, off results in a list containing parked and secured.

title: Tax Profile Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(records)` processing a list of tuples of income, age, and dependents. Determine the base tax profile string for each record and return them in a list. Income below thirty thousand is poverty line. Income between thirty thousand and sixty thousand is working class. Income between sixty thousand and one hundred thousand is middle class. Income above one hundred thousand is upper class. If age is over sixty five, append the string senior citizen. If age is under twenty five, append the string young adult. If dependents are zero, append the string single filer. If dependents are three or more, append the string large family. If income is over one hundred thousand and dependents are zero, append the string luxury tax candidate. Examples: an input tuple of twenty thousand, seventy, zero results in the string poverty line senior citizen single filer.

title: Train Fare Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(passengers)` taking a list of passenger tuples: age, day of week, travel class, and luggage count. Return a list of fare strings. Base status string is standard fare. Age under twelve makes it child fare. Age over sixty makes it senior fare. Age under five makes it infant free. Day is Saturday or Sunday appends the string weekend surcharge. Day is Friday appends the string peak travel fee. Class is first appends the string first class premium. Class is business appends the string business upgrade. Luggage over two appends the string excess baggage fee. Examples: an input tuple of ten, Monday, economy, zero results in the string child fare.

title: Medieval Weapon Classifier
spec: Write a function `identify(weapons)` processing a list of weapon specs: length, weight, blade presence, and pole presence. Return a classification string for each. If it has a blade and pole, it is a halberd. If it has a blade, no pole, and length over forty, it is a greatsword. If blade, no pole, length between twenty and forty, it is a longsword. If blade, no pole, length under twenty, it is a dagger. If no blade, pole, and length over sixty, it is a quarterstaff. If no blade, no pole, weight over ten, it is a warhammer. If no blade, no pole, weight between five and ten, it is a mace. If no blade, no pole, weight under five, it is a club. Otherwise return the string unknown weapon. Examples: an input tuple of thirty, four, true, false results in the string longsword.

title: Sushi Roll Describer
spec: Write a function `describe(rolls)` taking a list of ingredient lists for sushi rolls. Return a list containing the roll name string for each. Contains crab, avocado, and cucumber: california roll. Contains tuna and spicy mayo: spicy tuna roll. Contains eel, cucumber, and avocado: dragon roll. Contains salmon, cream cheese, and cucumber: philadelphia roll. Contains soft shell crab and avocado: spider roll. Contains shrimp tempura and cucumber: tempura roll. Contains yellowtail and scallion: yellowtail roll. Contains mixed sashimi and crab: rainbow roll. Otherwise return the string custom roll. Examples: an input list containing tuna and spicy mayo results in the string spicy tuna roll.

title: Garden Plant Recommender
spec: Write a function `recommend(conditions)` accepting a list of tuples: sunlight hours, soil acidity, and daily water volume. Recommend a plant type string for each. Sunlight over eight, low acidity, high water: tomatoes. Sunlight over eight, high acidity, moderate water: peppers. Sunlight over eight, low water: cacti. Sunlight under four, high water, low acidity: ferns. Sunlight under four, low water: snake plants. Sunlight between four and eight, high acidity, moderate water: blueberries. Sunlight between four and eight, low acidity, high water: hydrangeas. Sunlight between four and eight, low water: lavender. Otherwise return the string mixed grasses. Examples: an input tuple of nine, low, high results in the string tomatoes.

title: Medieval Title Generator
spec: Write a function `grant(subjects)` processing a list of tuples: gender, acres of land, and gold coins. Assign a title string to each. Gold over ten thousand, land over one thousand: duke for male, duchess for female. Gold over five thousand, land over five hundred: earl for male, countess for female. Gold over one thousand, land over one hundred: baron for male, baroness for female. Gold over five hundred, land over fifty: knight for male, dame for female. Land over ten, low gold: yeoman. Otherwise return the string peasant. Examples: an input tuple of male, two thousand, twelve thousand results in the string duke.

title: Astronomical Event Describer
spec: Write a function `observe(events)` processing a list of tuples: moon phase, eclipse status, meteor count, and comet presence. Describe each event returning a string. Moon is full, eclipse is lunar: blood moon. Moon is new, eclipse is solar: solar eclipse. Meteor count over fifty: meteor storm. Meteor count between ten and fifty: meteor shower. Comet is present: comet sighting. Moon is full, no eclipse, zero meteors: clear full moon. Moon is crescent, zero meteors: waxing crescent sky. Moon is new, zero meteors: dark sky observation. Otherwise return the string standard night sky. Examples: an input tuple of full, lunar, zero, false results in the string blood moon.

title: Ship Navigation Warning
spec: Write a function `navigate(hazards)` accepting a list of radar targets: distance, bearing, and speed. Return a warning priority level string for each. Distance under two, speed over twenty: collision imminent. Distance under two, speed under twenty: close quarters situation. Distance under five, bearing head on: evasive maneuvers required. Distance under five, bearing passing: maintain current course. Distance under ten, speed over ten: monitor target closely. Distance under ten, speed zero: stationary hazard ahead. Distance over twenty, speed over twenty: fast moving vessel distant. Distance over twenty, speed zero: clear waters. Otherwise return the string routine tracking. Examples: an input tuple of one, head on, twenty five results in the string collision imminent.

title: Pasta Shape Identifier
spec: Write a function `identify(pastas)` that accepts a list of pasta attributes, each a tuple of length, width, whether it is hollow, and whether it has ridges. Determine the pasta name string. If length is over two hundred, width is under two, and not hollow, it is spaghetti. If length is over two hundred, width is over five, and not hollow, it is fettuccine. If length is over two hundred and hollow, it is bucatini. If length is under fifty, hollow, and has ridges, it is rigatoni. If length is under fifty, hollow, and has no ridges, it is penne. If length is under twenty, not hollow, and has no ridges, it is orzo. If length is under fifty, width is over ten, and not hollow, it is pappardelle. Otherwise return the string unknown shape. Examples: an input tuple of thirty, fifteen, true, true results in the string rigatoni.

title: Perfume Scent Family
spec: Write a function `classify(perfumes)` processing a list of primary, secondary, and tertiary fragrance notes. Determine the scent family string for each. Primary is rose and secondary is jasmine: floral bouquet. Primary is lemon and secondary is bergamot: bright citrus. Primary is sandalwood and secondary is cedar: deep woody. Primary is vanilla and secondary is amber: oriental sweet. Primary is lavender and secondary is oakmoss: aromatic fougere. Primary is ocean breeze and tertiary is salt: marine aquatic. Primary is peach and secondary is plum: fruity lush. Primary is pepper and tertiary is clove: spicy warm. Otherwise return the string mixed blend. Examples: an input tuple of rose, jasmine, vanilla results in the string floral bouquet.

title: Martial Arts Belt Grader
spec: Write a function `grade(students)` taking a list of tuples: points, tournament wins, and training months. Return the belt color string. Points over one thousand and wins over ten: black belt. Points over eight hundred and wins over five: brown belt. Points over six hundred and training over twenty: red belt. Points over four hundred and wins over two: blue belt. Points over two hundred and training over twelve: green belt. Points over one hundred and training over six: orange belt. Points over fifty and training over three: yellow belt. Otherwise return white belt. If training is over sixty months and belt is not black, append the string dedicated student. Examples: an input tuple of eleven hundred, twelve, forty results in the string black belt.

title: Wine Pairing Recommender
spec: Write a function `pair(meals)` processing a list of tuples: main protein, sauce type, and spice level. Recommend a wine variety string. Protein is beef and sauce is heavy: cabernet sauvignon. Protein is beef and sauce is light: pinot noir. Protein is chicken and sauce is cream: chardonnay. Protein is chicken and sauce is tomato: sangiovese. Protein is fish and sauce is citrus: sauvignon blanc. Protein is pork and spice is high: riesling. Protein is lamb and spice is medium: syrah. Protein is duck and sauce is sweet: merlot. Otherwise return the string sparkling water. Examples: an input tuple of beef, heavy, low results in the string cabernet sauvignon.

title: Dinosaur Dietary Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify(dinosaurs)` processing a list of tuples: teeth type, posture, and size in meters. Determine the diet and family category string. Teeth are sharp, posture is bipedal, size over ten: large theropod carnivore. Teeth are sharp, posture is bipedal, size under ten: small theropod carnivore. Teeth are flat, posture is quadrupedal, size over twenty: huge sauropod herbivore. Teeth are flat, posture is quadrupedal, size under twenty: medium armored herbivore. Teeth are mixed, posture is bipedal, size under five: small omnivore. Teeth are flat, posture is bipedal, size over five: large ornithopod herbivore. Teeth are sharp, posture is aquatic: marine predator. Otherwise return the string unclassified specimen. Examples: an input tuple of sharp, bipedal, twelve results in the string large theropod carnivore.

title: Cheese Hardness Categorizer
spec: Write a function `categorize(cheeses)` processing a list of tuples: moisture percentage, aging months, and milk type. Determine the cheese category string. Moisture under thirty and aging over twelve: hard grating cheese. Moisture under forty and aging over six: firm sliceable cheese. Moisture between forty and fifty and aging under six: semi soft cheese. Moisture over fifty and aging under one: fresh spreadable cheese. Moisture over forty and milk is sheep: soft rind sheep cheese. Moisture over forty and milk is goat: fresh goat cheese. Moisture under thirty and milk is sheep: aged pecorino style. Otherwise return the string artisanal mixed cheese. Examples: an input tuple of twenty five, twenty, cow results in the string hard grating cheese.

title: Mythical Creature Identifier
spec: Write a function `identify(creatures)` processing a list of tuples: has wings, has horns, habitat, and breathes fire. Return the mythical creature string. Wings true, breathes fire true, habitat mountain: dragon. Wings true, breathes fire false, habitat forest: fairy. Wings false, horns true, habitat forest: unicorn. Wings false, horns true, habitat mountain: minotaur. Wings false, horns false, habitat ocean: mermaid. Wings false, horns false, habitat forest: elf. Wings true, horns false, habitat mountain: griffin. Wings true, horns true, habitat abyss: demon. Otherwise return the string unknown beast. Examples: an input tuple of true, false, mountain, true results in the string dragon.

title: Bread Type Describer
spec: Write a function `describe(breads)` taking a list of tuples: flour type, yeast present, and shape. Return the bread type string. Flour is wheat, yeast true, shape round: rustic boule. Flour is wheat, yeast true, shape long: traditional baguette. Flour is white, yeast true, shape square: sandwich loaf. Flour is rye, yeast true, shape oval: hearty pumpernickel. Flour is wheat, yeast false, shape flat: unleavened flatbread. Flour is corn, yeast false, shape square: classic cornbread. Flour is mixed, yeast true, shape braided: festive challah. Flour is white, yeast true, shape ring: chewy bagel. Otherwise return the string specialty bake. Examples: an input tuple of wheat, true, long results in the string traditional baguette.

title: Superhero Tier Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify(heroes)` processing a list of tuples: lifting strength in tons, flight speed in mach, and energy projection boolean. Return the superhero tier string. Strength over one hundred, speed over ten, energy true: cosmic tier. Strength over one hundred, speed under ten, energy false: planetary brute tier. Strength between fifty and one hundred, speed over five: global defender tier. Strength between ten and fifty, energy true: city protector tier. Strength under ten, speed under one, energy false: street level vigilante. Strength zero, speed zero, energy true: glass cannon mystic. Strength over fifty, speed zero, energy false: heavy tank tier. Otherwise return the string unranked hero. Examples: an input tuple of one hundred fifty, twelve, true results in the string cosmic tier.

title: Flower Arrangement Style
spec: Write a function `style(arrangements)` taking a list of tuples: vase shape, symmetry boolean, and dominant flower. Return the flower arrangement style string. Vase is tall, symmetry true, flower is rose: classic romantic style. Vase is low, symmetry false, flower is orchid: modern minimalist style. Vase is wide, symmetry true, flower is sunflower: rustic country style. Vase is tall, symmetry false, flower is lily: avant garde style. Vase is round, symmetry true, flower is peony: soft vintage style. Vase is low, symmetry true, flower is daisy: cheerful cottage style. Vase is tall, symmetry false, flower is branches: ikebana inspired style. Otherwise return the string eclectic mix. Examples: an input tuple of tall, true, rose results in the string classic romantic style.

title: Crystal Formation Identifier
spec: Write a function `identify(crystals)` processing a list of tuples: facet count, color clarity, and termination shape. Return the gemstone cut string. Facets over fifty, clarity is clear, shape is pointed: quartz point cluster. Facets over forty, clarity is opaque, shape is flat: banded agate slice. Facets over fifty, clarity is clear, shape is cubic: fluorite cube formation. Facets under twenty, clarity is clear, shape is stepped: bismuth hopper crystal. Facets under twenty, clarity is opaque, shape is round: polished jasper stone. Facets over fifty, clarity is opaque, shape is pointed: amethyst geode fragment. Facets over forty, clarity is clear, shape is hexagonal: beryl emerald prism. Facets under ten, clarity is opaque, shape is irregular: raw obsidian chunk. Otherwise return the string unknown mineral specimen. Examples: an input tuple of fifty eight, clear, pointed results in the string quartz point cluster.

title: Soup Category Identifier
spec: Write a function `identify(soups)` taking a list of tuples: base liquid, served hot boolean, and contains chunks boolean. Return the soup category string. Base is broth, hot true, chunks true: hearty stew. Base is broth, hot true, chunks false: clear consomme. Base is cream, hot true, chunks true: thick chowder. Base is cream, hot true, chunks false: smooth bisque. Base is tomato, hot false, chunks false: chilled gazpacho. Base is broth, hot false, chunks true: cold cucumber soup. Base is water, hot true, chunks true: rustic peasant soup. Base is milk, hot true, chunks false: warm milk broth. Otherwise return the string experimental soup. Examples: an input tuple of cream, true, true results in the string thick chowder.

title: Bridge Type Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify(bridges)` processing a list of tuples: span length in meters, primary material, and suspension cables boolean. Return the bridge type string. Span over one thousand, material steel, cables true: major suspension bridge. Span between five hundred and one thousand, material steel, cables true: cable stayed bridge. Span under five hundred, material steel, cables false: steel truss bridge. Span under one hundred, material wood, cables false: covered wooden bridge. Span under fifty, material stone, cables false: historic masonry arch. Span over one hundred, material concrete, cables false: concrete cantilever bridge. Span under twenty, material steel, cables false: simple beam bridge. Otherwise return the string custom span. Examples: an input tuple of twelve hundred, steel, true results in the string major suspension bridge.

title: Cloud Storage Tier
spec: Write a function `assign(buckets)` taking a list of tuples: size in gigabytes, access frequency per month, and multi region boolean. Return the storage tier string. Size over ten thousand, frequency over one thousand, multi region true: enterprise active global tier.
