Size over ten thousand, frequency over one thousand, multi region false: enterprise active local tier. Size over one thousand, frequency under ten, multi region true: deep archive global tier. Size over one thousand, frequency under ten, multi region false: deep archive local tier. Size under one thousand, frequency over one hundred, multi region false: standard frequent access tier. Size under one thousand, frequency under ten, multi region false: standard infrequent access tier. Size under ten, frequency over one thousand, multi region true: edge cached tier. Otherwise return the string unclassified storage tier. Examples: an input tuple of fifteen thousand, two thousand, true results in the string enterprise active global tier.

title: Renaissance Art Style
spec: Write a function `analyze(paintings)` processing a list of tuples: medium, perspective used boolean, and primary subject. Return the art style string. Medium is fresco, perspective true, subject is religion: high renaissance religious mural. Medium is oil, perspective true, subject is portrait: formal renaissance portraiture. Medium is tempera, perspective false, subject is religion: early renaissance altarpiece. Medium is oil, perspective true, subject is myth: classical mythology canvas. Medium is fresco, perspective false, subject is nature: decorative landscape fresco. Medium is oil, perspective false, subject is daily life: northern renaissance genre scene. Medium is sketch, perspective true, subject is architecture: architectural study. Otherwise return the string uncategorized artwork. Examples: an input tuple of fresco, true, religion results in the string high renaissance religious mural.

title: Spice Blend Identifier
spec: Write a function `identify(blends)` processing a list of ingredients. Return the spice blend name string. If it contains cumin, coriander, and turmeric, return curry powder. If it contains paprika, garlic, and oregano, return cajun seasoning. If it contains cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves, return pumpkin pie spice. If it contains basil, oregano, and rosemary, return italian seasoning. If it contains thyme, sesame, and sumac, return zaatar blend. If it contains chili powder, cumin, and oregano, return taco seasoning. If it contains black pepper, garlic, and onion, return everyday rub. If it contains star anise, fennel, and cloves, return five spice powder. Otherwise return the string unknown custom blend. Examples: an input list containing cumin, coriander, and turmeric results in the string curry powder.

title: Camera Sensor Format
spec: Write a function `sensor(width, height)` that takes two numeric dimensions representing a camera sensor in millimeters and returns its common format name as a plain lowercase string. If the dimensions are thirty six and twenty four, return full frame. If they are twenty three and fifteen, return apsc. For seventeen and thirteen, return micro four thirds. For forty four and thirty three, return medium format. For fifty three and forty, return large format. For thirteen and eight, return one inch. For five and four, return mobile sensor. If the dimensions do not match any known format, return unknown format. Example: width thirty six and height twenty four should result in the text full frame.

title: Historical Sword Classifier
spec: Create a function `sword(blade, edge, curve)` that classifies historical swords based on blade length in inches, number of sharp edges, and whether the blade is curved. If the length is between twenty and thirty, with two edges and straight, return gladius. If length is thirty to forty, two edges and straight, return longsword. If length is above forty, two edges and straight, return claymore. If length is thirty to forty, one edge and curved, return sabre. If length is twenty to thirty, one edge and curved, return scimitar. If length is above thirty, one edge and slightly curved, return katana. If length is thirty to forty, two edges but very narrow, return rapier. If it does not match any of these, return unknown weapon. Example: thirty five, two, false returns longsword.

title: Engine Cylinder Layout
spec: Implement a function `engine(cylinders, angle)` that identifies the layout of an internal combustion engine based on the number of cylinders and the angle between banks in degrees. If the angle is zero and cylinders are four or six, return straight four or straight six respectively. If the angle is sixty or ninety, and cylinders are six or eight, return v six or v eight. If the angle is one hundred eighty, return flat four for four cylinders, or flat six for six cylinders. If the angle is fifteen and cylinders are sixteen, return w sixteen. If the angle is seventy two and cylinders are twelve, return v twelve. For any other combination, return custom layout. Example: six cylinders and angle sixty returns v six.

title: Video Connector Identifier
spec: Design a function `connector(pins, shape, digital)` that takes an integer pin count, a description of the plug shape, and a boolean indicating if the signal is digital, returning the standard display connection type. If pins are fifteen, shape is d sub, and digital is false, return vga. If pins are twenty nine, shape is rectangular, and digital is true, return dvi. If pins are nineteen, shape is trapezoid, and digital is true, return hdmi. If pins are twenty, shape is notched rectangle, and digital is true, return displayport. If pins are four, shape is circular, and digital is false, return s video. If pins are three, shape is circular, and digital is false, return component. If pins are twenty four, shape is rectangular, and digital is true, return usb c. Otherwise, return proprietary. Example: nineteen, trapezoid, true returns hdmi.

title: Plumbing Pipe Material
spec: Write a function `pipe(color, rigid, metal)` that determines the material of a plumbing pipe based on its external color, whether it is completely rigid, and whether it is metallic. If the pipe is metallic, rigid, and reddish brown, return copper. If metallic, rigid, and silver or grey, return galvanized steel. If metallic, rigid, and black, return black iron. If non metallic, rigid, and white, return pvc. If non metallic, rigid, and beige, return cpvc. If non metallic, flexible, and blue or red, return pex. If non metallic, flexible, and black, return polyethylene. If non metallic, rigid, and black, return abs. For anything else, return unidentified pipe. Example: white, true, false returns pvc.

title: Roof Style Classifier
spec: Develop a function `roof(slopes, flat)` that identifies architectural roof styles based on the number of sloping sides and whether there is a completely flat section on top. If there are two slopes and no flat section, return gable. If there are four slopes and no flat section, return hip. If there are two slopes and a flat top, return gambrel. If there are four slopes and a flat top, return mansard. If there is only one slope, return shed. If there are zero slopes and it is completely flat, return flat roof. If there are more than four slopes forming a circle, return conical. If the slopes form an inverted v shape towards the middle, return butterfly. Example: four, false returns hip.

title: Window Type Identifier
spec: Create a function `window(hinges, slides, opens)` that classifies common residential windows based on hinge location, sliding direction, and whether it opens outward or inward. If it does not slide, has hinges on the side, and opens outward, return casement. If it has hinges on the top and opens outward, return awning. If it has hinges on the bottom and opens inward, return hopper. If it slides vertically and only the bottom half moves, return single hung. If it slides vertically and both halves move, return double hung. If it slides horizontally, return slider. If it does not slide, has no hinges, and does not open, return picture window. If it has multiple glass louvers that tilt, return jalousie. Example: side, false, outward returns casement.

title: Motorcycle Style Categorizer
spec: Write a function `motorcycle(posture, fairing, clearance)` that categorizes motorbikes based on the rider posture, presence of plastic fairings, and ground clearance. If the posture is forward leaning, fairing is full, and clearance is low, return sportbike. If the posture is laid back, fairing is none, and clearance is low, return cruiser. If posture is upright, fairing is partial, and clearance is high, return adventure. If posture is upright, fairing is none, and clearance is moderate, return standard. If posture is standing, fairing is none, and clearance is very high, return dirt bike. If posture is upright, fairing is full, and clearance is low, return touring. If posture is forward leaning, fairing is none, and clearance is low, return cafe racer. If it does not match, return custom build. Example: laid back, none, low returns cruiser.

title: Archery Bow Type
spec: Implement a function `bow(cams, recurved, length)` that determines the type of archery bow based on the number of mechanical cams, whether the limbs curve away from the archer, and the overall length in inches. If there are two cams, return compound bow. If there are zero cams, the limbs are recurved, and length is under sixty, return horse bow. If zero cams, recurved limbs, and length is above sixty, return olympic recurve. If zero cams, straight limbs, and length is above seventy, return english longbow. If zero cams, straight limbs, and length is under sixty, return flatbow. If the length is under thirty and it mounts horizontally, return crossbow. If it uses a distinct asymmetrical shape over eighty inches, return yumi. Otherwise, return traditional bow. Example: two, false, forty returns compound bow.

title: Mattress Size Dimensioner
spec: Design a function `mattress(width, length)` that takes the dimensions of a bed in inches and returns the standard US mattress size name. If the dimensions are thirty eight by seventy five, return twin. If thirty eight by eighty, return twin xl. If fifty four by seventy five, return full. If sixty by eighty, return queen. If seventy six by eighty, return king. If seventy two by eighty four, return california king. If sixty six by eighty, return olympic queen. If eighty four by eighty four, return wyoming king. If the dimensions do not match any standard size, return custom size. Example: sixty and eighty returns queen.

title: Shoe Toe Shape
spec: Write a function `toe(taper, width, box)` that categorizes the toe shape of dress shoes based on the degree of taper, the overall width at the tip, and whether the front is boxed off. If taper is extreme and width is very narrow, return pointed. If taper is moderate, width is narrow, and the tip is slightly rounded, return almond. If taper is slight and width is wide with a curved front, return round. If taper is minimal and the front is completely flat, return square. If taper is moderate but the very tip is chopped off flat, return snip toe. If there is a distinct u shaped seam on top, return moc toe. If the toe features wing shaped leather layers, return wingtip. If none apply, return plain toe. Example: extreme, very narrow, false returns pointed.

title: Keyboard Layout Analyzer
spec: Create a function `keyboard(toprow)` that identifies the language or typing layout of a computer keyboard based on the first six letters of the top alphabetical row. If the string is q w e r t y, return standard american. If it is q w e r t z, return central european. If it is a z e r t y, return standard french. If it is d v o r a k, return dvorak simplified. If it is q w f p g j, return colemak. If it is x v l c w k, return bepo. If it is a s d f g h, return home row testing. If the string does not match these, return unrecognized layout. Example: q w e r t z returns central european.

title: Guitar Body Style
spec: Develop a function `guitar(horns, hollow, shape)` that determines an electric or acoustic guitar body style based on the number of cutaway horns, whether the body is hollow, and the general outline. If it has two asymmetric horns, is solid, and rounded, return stratocaster style. If it has one small horn, is solid, and rounded, return telecaster style. If it has one horn, is solid, and carved top, return les paul style. If it has two symmetric pointed horns, is solid, return sg style. If it is an inverted v shape, return flying v. If it is a jagged angular shape, return explorer style. If it is hollow with f holes and two horns, return es style. If it is completely hollow with no horns and a thick waist, return dreadnought. Example: two asymmetric horns, false, rounded returns stratocaster style.

title: Drum Kit Component
spec: Implement a function `drum(diameter, depth, metallic)` that classifies a piece of a drum set based on its diameter in inches, depth in inches, and whether it is a metallic cymbal. If it is metallic, fourteen inches, and mounted in pairs, return hi hat. If metallic, sixteen to eighteen inches, return crash cymbal. If metallic, twenty to twenty two inches, return ride cymbal. If non metallic, fourteen inches wide, and shallow depth around five, return snare drum. If non metallic, twenty to twenty four inches wide, and deep, return bass drum. If non metallic, ten to twelve inches wide, return rack tom. If non metallic, sixteen inches wide and deep, return floor tom. For any other dimensions, return custom percussion. Example: twenty, deep, false returns bass drum.

title: Book Binding Type
spec: Write a function `binding(cover, pages, glued)` that takes a cover type, page attachment method, and a boolean for glue usage to determine a book binding style. If the cover is hardcover, pages are sewn, and glued is true, return case binding. If cover is softcover, pages are individual, and glued is true, return perfect binding. If cover is softcover, pages are folded, and glued is false with staples, return saddle stitch. If cover is bare boards, pages are sewn, and glued is false, return coptic stitch. If pages are held by a continuous coiled wire, return spiral binding. If held by a metal comb with double loops, return wire o binding. If held by a plastic spine with teeth, return comb binding. Otherwise, return custom bind. Example: softcover, individual, true returns perfect binding.

title: Bread Scoring Pattern
spec: Design a function `scoring(slashes, angle, overlapping)` that evaluates the decorative cuts on an artisan bread loaf. If there is one slash at a shallow angle, return ear slash. If there are two intersecting slashes at right angles, return cross. If there are four overlapping slashes forming a grid, return tic tac toe. If there are multiple small slashes radiating from a central curved line, return wheat stalk. If there are four slashes forming a rectangle, return box score. If there are multiple slashes forming a diamond pattern, return diamond grid. If there is a single curved slash mimicking the edge, return crescent. If there are no slashes, return rustic split. Example: two, perpendicular, true returns cross.

title: Sandwich Style Classifier
spec: Create a function `sandwich(bread, meat, cheese)` that identifies a classic sandwich based on its core ingredients. If bread is rye, meat is corned beef, and cheese is swiss, return reuben. If bread is hoagie, meat is shaved steak, and cheese is provolone, return philly cheesesteak. If bread is baguette, meat is pate and pork, and cheese is none, return banh mi. If bread is white, meat is bacon, and cheese is none, return blt. If bread is cuban, meat is roast pork and ham, and cheese is swiss, return cubano. If bread is pita, meat is lamb, and cheese is feta, return gyro. If bread is sourdough, meat is turkey, and cheese is cheddar, return turkey melt. Otherwise, return generic sandwich. Example: hoagie, shaved steak, provolone returns philly cheesesteak.

title: Gemstone Cut Style
spec: Write a function `gemcut(shape, facets, stepped)` that takes the outline shape, number of facets, and a boolean for whether the facets are parallel stepped lines to identify a jewelry cut. If the shape is round, facets are fifty seven, and stepped is false, return round brilliant. If the shape is square, facets are fifty to fifty eight, and stepped is false, return princess cut. If the shape is rectangular with truncated corners and stepped is true, return emerald cut. If the shape is square with truncated corners and stepped is true, return asscher cut. If the shape is oval with pointed ends and stepped is false, return marquise cut. If the shape is a teardrop and stepped is false, return pear cut. If the shape is a rounded rectangle and stepped is false, return cushion cut. If the shape is a triangle with flat edges, return trilliant cut. For anything else, return fantasy cut. Example: rectangular, fifty, true returns emerald cut.

title: Pen Nib Type
spec: Implement a function `nib(width, flexibility, flat)` that classifies fountain pen writing tips based on their line width in millimeters, whether they yield under pressure, and if the tip is ground flat. If the width is under zero point four, firm, and not flat, return extra fine. If the width is around zero point five, firm, and not flat, return fine. If the width is zero point seven, firm, and not flat, return medium. If the width is zero point nine, firm, and not flat, return broad. If the tip is flat and firm, return stub. If the tip is flat and flexible, return italic. If the tip is not flat but highly flexible, return flex nib. If the tip is bent upwards for variable angles, return fude. Example: flat, firm returns stub.

title: Ergonomic Chair Classifier
spec: Write a function `chair(lumbar, armrests, tilt)` that categorizes office seating based on back support, arm style, and recline mechanism. If lumbar is fixed, armrests are fixed, and tilt is center, return basic task chair. If lumbar is adjustable, armrests are three dimensional, and tilt is synchronized, return ergonomic chair. If lumbar is none, armrests are fixed loops, and tilt is knee tilt, return conference chair. If lumbar is none, armrests are none, and tilt is absent, return drafting stool. If lumbar is aggressive, armrests are flip up, and tilt is lockable, return gaming chair. If lumbar is dynamic, armrests are four dimensional, and tilt is weight sensitive, return premium executive. If lumbar is none, armrests are none, and tilt is center, return typing chair. If none apply, return custom seating. Example: adjustable, three dimensional, synchronized returns ergonomic chair.

title: Vacuum Cleaner Style
spec: Create a function `vacuum(corded, bag, form)` that determines the type of household floor cleaner based on power supply, dirt collection method, and physical form factor. If corded is true, bag is true, and form is vertical, return bagged upright. If corded is true, bag is false, and form is vertical, return bagless upright. If corded is true, bag is true, and form is horizontal box, return bagged canister. If corded is false, bag is false, and form is wand, return cordless stick. If corded is false, bag is false, and form is robotic disc, return robot vacuum. If corded is true, bag is false, and form is heavy duty barrel, return shop vac. If corded is false, bag is false, and form is handheld, return dustbuster. If corded is false, bag is true, and form is backpack, return commercial backpack. For any other combination, return unspecified vacuum. Example: true, true, vertical returns bagged upright.

title: Fireplace Fuel Type
spec: Develop a function `fireplace(chimney, flame, starter)` that classifies a hearth heating appliance based on whether it requires a vertical chimney, the flame appearance, and the ignition method. If it requires a chimney, flame is yellow and crackling, and starter is match, return wood burning. If it requires a chimney, flame is steady blue and yellow, and starter is pilot light, return vented gas. If it does not require a chimney, flame is steady, and starter is piezo, return ventless gas. If it requires no chimney, flame is an optical illusion, and starter is remote control, return electric fireplace. If it requires no chimney, flame is low and real, and starter is gel can, return ethanol burner. If it requires a massive masonry chimney and starter is kindling, return traditional hearth. If it uses pellets with an electric auger, return pellet stove. If it uses coal and has a lower grate, return coal stove. Otherwise, return decorative mantel. Example: true, yellow and crackling, match returns wood burning.

title: Eyeglass Frame Style
spec: Implement a function `eyeglass(rim, material, bridge)` that categorizes spectacles based on rim enclosure, build material, and nose bridge style. If rim is full, material is thick plastic, and bridge is keyhole, return retro acetate. If rim is half, material is metal, and bridge is adjustable pads, return browline. If rim is none, material is titanium, and bridge is saddle, return rimless. If rim is full, material is wire, and bridge is double, return aviator. If rim is full, material is thin plastic, and bridge is saddle, return classic square. If rim is full, material is tortoise shell, and bridge is keyhole, return vintage round. If rim is half, material is thick plastic, and bridge is saddle, return clubmaster. If it does not match these, return generic optical. Example: half, metal, adjustable pads returns browline.

title: Boat Hull Design
spec: Write a function `hull(bottom, chines, beam)` that takes the shape of a boat's underside, the sharpness of its side angles, and its width ratio to identify the hull category. If the bottom is flat, chines are hard, and beam is wide, return flat bottom skiff. If the bottom is completely round, chines are soft, and beam is narrow, return displacement hull. If the bottom is a deep v shape, chines are hard, and beam is moderate, return deep v planing. If the bottom is a shallow v, chines are hard, and beam is wide, return modified v. If the bottom features two distinct parallel tubes, return catamaran. If the bottom has a central main hull and two small outer outriggers, return trimaran. If the bottom has stepping ridges, return stepped hull. If bottom is perfectly flat and beam is extremely narrow, return racing shell. Otherwise, return custom hull. Use a helper for extreme cases: if tire width is over one hundred, return the phrase fat bike snow float. Then determine the pressure. If rough terrain is true and width is above fifty, return the phrase low pressure trail grip. If rough terrain is true and width is below thirty, return the phrase medium pressure gravel. If rough terrain is false and width is below twenty five, return the phrase high pressure track racing. If rough terrain is false and width is between twenty five and thirty five, return the phrase firm pressure road commute. If weight is over one hundred and rough terrain is true, return the phrase reinforced sidewall pressure. If weight is under fifty, return the phrase extra soft comfort pressure. Otherwise, return the phrase standard mixed surface pressure. Include a small driver block.

title: House Plant Light
spec: Write a function `advise(plant)` that takes a list containing an integer for leaf thickness, an integer for variegation percentage, and a boolean for flowering. If leaf thickness is negative, return the phrase impossible leaf measurement. If variegation is over one hundred, return the phrase invalid variegation amount. Use a helper for blooms: if flowering is true, return the phrase bright direct sun required. Then determine light needs. If leaf thickness is above ten and variegation is above fifty, return the phrase bright indirect light. If leaf thickness is above ten and variegation is below twenty, return the phrase medium indirect light. If leaf thickness is below five and variegation is above fifty, return the phrase morning sun dappled shade. If leaf thickness is below five and variegation is below twenty, return the phrase low light tolerant shade. If leaf thickness is exactly zero, return the phrase artificial grow light only. If variegation is exactly zero, return the phrase deep shade survivor. Otherwise, return the phrase standard room lighting. Add a test driver.

title: Salad Dressing Mixer
spec: Write a function `blend(ingredients)` taking a list with an integer for oil percentage, an integer for vinegar percentage, and a boolean for dairy included. If oil or vinegar is negative, return the phrase invalid negative percentages. If the sum of oil and vinegar exceeds one hundred, return the phrase proportions exceed maximum. Create a helper for dairy: if dairy is true and oil is above fifty, return the phrase creamy classic ranch; if dairy is true and oil is fifty or below, return the phrase tangy blue cheese. Then determine the vinaigrette. If oil is above seventy and vinegar is below twenty, return the phrase mild olive oil dressing. If oil is between fifty and seventy and vinegar is above twenty, return the phrase sharp balsamic vinaigrette. If oil is below fifty and vinegar is above forty, return the phrase acidic red wine vinaigrette. If oil is exactly fifty and vinegar is exactly fifty, return the phrase perfectly balanced emulsion. If oil is below twenty, return the phrase light citrus splash. For all other combinations, return the phrase standard house vinaigrette. Add a test driver.

title: Bird Feeder Selector
spec: Write a function `select(birds)` receiving a list with an integer for target bird size, an integer for squirrel presence, and a boolean for clinging ability. If size or squirrel presence is negative, return the phrase invalid negative metrics. If squirrel presence exceeds ten, return the phrase extreme squirrel warning. Use a helper for special feeding: if clinging ability is true and size is under five, return the phrase upside down suet cage. Then determine the feeder. If squirrel presence is above seven and size is under ten, return the phrase weight sensitive tube feeder. If squirrel presence is above seven and size is over ten, return the phrase baffled pole platform. If squirrel presence is below four and size is over fifteen, return the phrase open ground feeding tray. If squirrel presence is below four and clinging ability is true, return the phrase mesh peanut wreath. If clinging ability is false and size is under ten, return the phrase wooden hopper feeder. If size is exactly zero, return the phrase liquid hummingbird nectar. Otherwise, return the phrase standard mixed seed feeder. Include a small driver block.

title: Skincare Routine Builder
spec: Write a function `build(skin)` taking a list with an integer for oiliness level, an integer for sensitivity level, and a boolean for morning routine. If oiliness or sensitivity is negative, return the phrase levels cannot be negative. If both levels exceed ten, return the phrase extreme dermatological condition. Use a helper for morning care: if morning routine is true and sensitivity is above seven, return the phrase gentle mineral daily sunscreen; if morning routine is true, return the phrase lightweight chemical sunscreen. For evening routines: if oiliness is above eight and sensitivity is below four, return the phrase strong exfoliating acid toner. If oiliness is above eight and sensitivity is above seven, return the phrase soothing salicylic wash. If oiliness is below four and sensitivity is below four, return the phrase thick rich night moisturizer. If oiliness is below four and sensitivity is above seven, return the phrase hypoallergenic repairing ceramide cream. If oiliness is exactly five and sensitivity is exactly five, return the phrase balanced hydrating face serum. Otherwise, return the phrase mild purifying clay mask. Include a short test driver.

title: Camping Tent Material
spec: Write a function `choose(weather)` that accepts a list with an integer for expected rainfall, an integer for carrying weight limit, and a boolean for winter conditions. If rainfall or weight limit is negative, return the phrase invalid negative conditions. If rainfall exceeds one hundred, return the phrase flood warning extreme condition. Create a helper for winter: if winter conditions are true, return the phrase heavy cotton canvas four season. Then evaluate the materials. If rainfall is above fifty and weight limit is under five, return the phrase expensive cuben fiber ultralight. If rainfall is above fifty and weight limit is over ten, return the phrase durable coated polyester dome. If rainfall is under twenty and weight limit is under three, return the phrase ultralight silnylon tarp. If rainfall is under twenty and weight limit is over ten, return the phrase cheap polyethylene festival tent. If rainfall is exactly zero and weight limit is under five, return the phrase mesh insect net only. If weight limit is exactly zero, return the phrase reflective thermal bivy sack. For all other inputs, return the phrase breathable waterproof membrane. Include a test driver block.

title: Guitar String Gauge
spec: Write a function `recommend(guitar)` that takes a list with an integer for tuning pitch drop, an integer for player hand strength, and a boolean for acoustic instrument. If tuning drop or hand strength is negative, return the phrase invalid negative specifications. If tuning drop exceeds twelve, return the phrase extreme down tuning not supported. Create a helper for acoustic guitars: if acoustic instrument is true and hand strength is under five, return the phrase silk and steel folk strings; if acoustic instrument is true, return the phrase standard phosphor bronze medium. Then analyze electric guitars. If tuning drop is above four and hand strength is above seven, return the phrase baritone heavy tension gauge. If tuning drop is above four and hand strength is under five, return the phrase drop tuning medium gauge. If tuning drop is zero and hand strength is under three, return the phrase extra light flexible gauge. If tuning drop is zero and hand strength is above eight, return the phrase heavy tension jazz strings. If tuning drop is two, return the phrase regular light gauge hybrid. Otherwise, return the phrase standard medium tension gauge. Add a test driver.

title: Paint Roller Nap
spec: Write a function `determine(surface)` taking a list with an integer for wall roughness, an integer for paint glossiness, and a boolean for exterior use. If roughness or glossiness is negative, return the phrase negative measurements invalid. If glossiness exceeds one hundred, return the phrase gloss level exceeds maximum. Use a helper for outside work: if exterior use is true and roughness is above fifty, return the phrase thick sheepskin exterior roller. Then analyze interior needs. If roughness is under ten and glossiness is above eighty, return the phrase foam cabinet ultra smooth finish. If roughness is under ten and glossiness is under twenty, return the phrase very smooth microfiber roller. If roughness is between ten and thirty and glossiness is above fifty, return the phrase semi smooth woven roller. If roughness is between ten and thirty and glossiness is under twenty, return the phrase semi smooth knit roller. If roughness is between thirty and sixty, return the phrase semi rough surface nap. If roughness is above sixty, return the phrase rough texture long nap. Otherwise, return the phrase standard all purpose medium nap. Add a driver block.

title: Sailing Knot Suggester
spec: Write a function `suggest(rigging)` that receives a list with an integer for load weight, an integer for rope thickness, and a boolean for quick release needed. If load or thickness is negative, return the phrase invalid negative parameters. If load exceeds one thousand, return the phrase extreme load danger warning. Create a helper for emergencies: if quick release needed is true, return the phrase slippery highwayman hitch. Then determine the standard knot. If load is above five hundred and thickness is over twenty, return the phrase heavy duty bowline loop. If load is above five hundred and thickness is under ten, return the phrase reinforced double figure eight. If load is under one hundred and thickness is over twenty, return the phrase bulky clove hitch tying. If load is under one hundred and thickness is under ten, return the phrase standard flat reef knot. If load is exactly zero, return the phrase decorative monkey fist knot. If thickness is exactly zero, return the phrase invisible thread whipping knot. For all other combinations, return the phrase adjustable taut line hitch. Provide a driver block.

title: Mattress Firmness Rater
spec: Write a function `rate(sleeper)` taking a list with an integer for body weight, an integer for back pain level, and a boolean for side sleeper. If weight or back pain is negative, return the phrase negative attributes not permitted. If back pain exceeds ten, return the phrase severe pain requires medical advice. Use a helper for sleeping position: if side sleeper is true and weight is under sixty, return the phrase extra plush soft contouring. Then evaluate back and stomach sleepers. If weight is over one hundred and back pain is above seven, return the phrase extra firm orthopedic support. If weight is over one hundred and back pain is below four, return the phrase traditional firm support. If weight is between sixty and one hundred and back pain is above seven, return the phrase luxury firm balanced relief. If weight is between sixty and one hundred and back pain is below four, return the phrase medium plush comfort foam. If weight is under sixty and back pain is above seven, return the phrase dual zone split firmness. If weight is exactly zero, return the phrase zero gravity suspension bed. Otherwise, return the phrase latex bouncy responsive medium. Add a small driver.

title: Firewood Type Recommender
spec: Write a function `recommend(fire)` accepting a list with an integer for desired burn time, an integer for heat output required, and a boolean for cooking food. If burn time or heat output is negative, return the phrase invalid negative requirements. If burn time exceeds twenty four, return the phrase dangerously long unattended burn. Create a helper for cooking: if cooking food is true and heat output is above five, return the phrase sweet smelling cherry wood; if cooking food is true, return the phrase mild smoking apple wood. For heating fires: if burn time is above ten and heat output is above eight, return the phrase slow burning dense oak. If burn time is above ten and heat output is below four, return the phrase soft burning white ash. If burn time is under five and heat output is above eight, return the phrase hot burning hickory logs. If burn time is under five and heat output is below four, return the phrase quick starting white birch. If burn time is exactly one, return the phrase popping cedar kindling wood. For all other cases, return the phrase resinous fragrant pine logs. Include a test driver.

title: Bread Dough Hydration
spec: Write a function `calculate(recipe)` that takes a list with an integer for ambient temperature, an integer for resting time, and a boolean for whole grain flour. If temperature or resting time is negative, return the phrase impossible negative environment. If resting time exceeds seventy two, return the phrase excessive fermentation risk. Use a helper for flour type: if whole grain flour is true and resting time is above twenty four, return the phrase whole wheat extreme hydration. Then determine the dough type. If temperature is above thirty and resting time is under two, return the phrase stiff bagel dough mix. If temperature is above thirty and resting time is over twelve, return the phrase liquid batter starter poolish. If temperature is below fifteen and resting time is over twenty four, return the phrase cold ferment artisan rustic. If temperature is below fifteen and resting time is under five, return the phrase dense heavy pretzel dough. If temperature is exactly twenty and resting time is exactly twelve, return the phrase standard sandwich loaf dough. If resting time is zero, return the phrase immediate bake unleavened flatbread. For any other combination, return the phrase wet ciabatta slipper dough. Include a driver block.

title: Train Delay Announcer
spec: Write a program with the entry function `announce(minutes)` that generates an announcement for train delays. Map delays to phrases: zero is on time, one to five is minor delays, six to fifteen is moderate delays, sixteen to thirty is significant delays. For thirty one to fifty nine use severe delays, exactly sixty is one hour delay, anything higher is indefinite delay, and negative is invalid time. Include a helper function that prepends the phrase attention passengers to any valid delay announcement. Examples: announce(4) returns "attention passengers minor delays", announce(60) returns "attention passengers one hour delay".

title: Burger Meal Assembler
spec: Create a program starting with `assemble(number)` that returns a list of strings representing items in a fast food combo meal. Number one returns the classic burger, regular fries, and a cola. Number two returns a cheeseburger, curly fries, and an orange soda, while number three gives a double burger, onion rings, and a root beer. Number four yields a veggie burger, a side salad, and iced tea, and number five gives a chicken sandwich, waffle fries, and lemonade. Any other number should return a list containing just the word water. Examples: assemble(2) returns ["cheeseburger", "curly fries", "orange soda"], assemble(9) returns ["water"].

title: Zodiac Element Mapper
spec: Develop a module with the function `element(sign)` that maps an astrological sign to its classical element string. Aries, leo, and sagittarius map to the word fire, while taurus, virgo, and capricorn map to the word earth. Gemini, libra, and aquarius produce the word air, and cancer, scorpio, and pisces yield the word water. If the sign is not recognized, return the phrase unknown element. Include a helper routine that takes a list of signs and returns a list of their corresponding elements. Examples: element("aries") returns "fire", element("libra") returns "air".

title: Tarot Arcana Classifier
spec: Design a script featuring `arcana(card)` that categorizes a tarot card into its correct arcana group. The fool, the magician, the high priestess, the empress, and the emperor belong to the major arcana. The ace of wands, two of cups, three of swords, and four of pentacles belong to the minor arcana. If the input matches a card from the first group, return the phrase major arcana, and for the second group return the phrase minor arcana. For any other card, return the phrase card not found, and provide a helper that filters a list of cards to return only major arcana ones. Examples: arcana("the fool") returns "major arcana", arcana("three of swords") returns "minor arcana".

title: Fantasy Gear Slot Mapper
spec: Write a utility with the main function `equip(item)` that determines where a piece of fantasy equipment is worn on a character. Broadswords and daggers are worn in the primary hand, shields and lanterns in the secondary hand, and helmets and crowns on the head. Breastplates and tunics go on the chest, gauntlets and gloves on the hands, boots and sandals on the feet, capes and cloaks on the back, and rings and bracelets in the accessories slot. Return the appropriate slot name for the item, or the word inventory if the item is not recognized. Examples: equip("shield") returns "secondary hand", equip("crown") returns "head".

title: Waste Disposal Categorizer
spec: Implement a tool with the function `sort(material)` that directs a user to the correct waste bin for an item. Cardboard and newspaper go into the blue bin, glass bottles and aluminum cans into the yellow bin, and apple cores and coffee grounds into the green bin. Plastic bags and styrofoam belong in the grey bin, old batteries and light bulbs in the hazardous waste bin, and old clothing in the donation bin. Any other material should return the phrase landfill bin. Examples: sort("newspaper") returns "blue bin", sort("apple cores") returns "green bin".

title: Fabric Stain Treatment
spec: Create a guide accessed via `treat(stain)` that suggests a cleaning method for various fabric stains. Coffee and tea require boiling water and vinegar, red wine requires salt and club soda, and grease or oil requires dish soap and baking soda. Ink needs rubbing alcohol, grass needs hydrogen peroxide, blood needs cold water and ammonia, makeup needs shaving cream, and dirt or mud requires dry brushing and detergent. If the stain is completely unknown, return the phrase professional dry cleaning. Examples: treat("ink") returns "rubbing alcohol", treat("red wine") returns "salt and club soda".

title: Seed Planting Season
spec: Write a program with `plant(crop)` that returns the best season to sow specific vegetable seeds. Peas, spinach, and radishes should return the word spring, while tomatoes, peppers, and eggplants return the word summer. Kale, carrots, and turnips return the word autumn, and garlic, onions, and winter wheat return the word winter. Include a helper that takes a season and returns the warning frost danger if it is winter, otherwise it should return good growing conditions. If the crop is unknown, return the word greenhouse. Examples: plant("tomatoes") returns "summer", plant("peas") returns "spring".

title: Orchestra Section Locator
spec: Develop a mapping tool using `seat(instrument)` that returns the proper orchestra section for a given musical instrument. Violin, viola, cello, and double bass belong to the string section, whereas flute, oboe, clarinet, and bassoon belong to the woodwind section. Trumpet, french horn, trombone, and tuba make up the brass section. Timpani, snare drum, xylophone, and cymbals go to the percussion section, and piano and harpsichord belong to the keyboard section. If the instrument is not found, return the phrase guest soloist. Examples: seat("cello") returns "string section", seat("oboe") returns "woodwind section".

title: Pet Show Category
spec: Implement a function `show(animal)` that categorizes pets into competition groups for a local animal exhibition. Golden retrievers, poodles, and beagles go into the sporting dogs category, while persian, siamese, and maine coon cats go into the pedigree cats category. Parrots, canaries, and finches fall under the avian category, hamsters, guinea pigs, and rabbits under the small mammals category. Snakes, lizards, and turtles belong to the reptile category, and goldfish, bettas, and guppies fit into the aquatic category. Any other animal returns the phrase general exhibition. Examples: show("beagle") returns "sporting dogs", show("parrot") returns "avian".

title: Theme Park Ride Height
spec: Create a safety checker with `allow(ride)` that returns the minimum height requirement phrase for various amusement park attractions. The roller coaster and the drop tower require the phrase tall enough for thrill rides. The ferris wheel and the carousel require the phrase safe for all heights. The bumper cars and the haunted house require the phrase medium height required, while the water slide requires the phrase tall enough for water rides. Any unknown ride should default to returning the phrase check with operator. Examples: allow("roller coaster") returns "tall enough for thrill rides", allow("carousel") returns "safe for all heights".

title: Fossil Era Mapper
spec: Write a geological script anchored by `era(fossil)` that returns the geological era when a specific prehistoric creature lived. Trilobites and anomalocaris return the paleozoic era, while stegosaurus, triceratops, and tyrannosaurus return the mesozoic era. Mammoths, saber toothed cats, and dire wolves return the cenozoic era, ediacaran biota returns the neoproterozoic era, and cyanobacteria returns the archean eon. Include a helper function that takes an era string and appends the suffix fossil record to the end of it. Unknown fossils should simply return the phrase unclassified timeline. Examples: era("trilobites") returns "paleozoic era", era("mammoths") returns "cenozoic era".

title: Athletics Event Group
spec: Design an organizer with `group(event)` that categorizes standard track and field events. The hundred meter sprint, two hundred meter dash, and four hundred meter run fall under the sprints category, while the eight hundred meter and fifteen hundred meter are classified as middle distance. The five thousand meter and ten thousand meter are long distance, and hurdles and steeplechase are obstacle events. High jump, pole vault, long jump, and triple jump are jumping events, and shot put, discus, hammer, and javelin are throwing events. Any other event returns the decathlon category. Examples: group("high jump") returns "jumping events", group("shot put") returns "throwing events".

title: Beverage Glassware Matcher
spec: Develop a bartender assistant function `serve(drink)` that returns the appropriate glass type for a classic beverage. A martini or manhattan gets a cocktail glass, a margarita gets a margarita glass, and a whiskey or bourbon gets a rocks glass. A champagne or prosecco gets a flute, a red wine or white wine gets a wine glass, and a pilsner or stout gets a pint glass. A hot toddy or irish coffee is served in a mug. Any unknown drink defaults to a highball glass. Examples: serve("martini") returns "cocktail glass", serve("stout") returns "pint glass".

title: Noodle Dish Classifier
spec: Implement a culinary guide `noodle(dish)` that identifies the cultural base cuisine of a popular noodle dish. Pad thai, drunken noodles, and pad see ew return the word thai. Pho and bun bo hue return the word vietnamese, while ramen, udon, and soba return the word japanese. Spaghetti, fettuccine, and penne return the word italian, chow mein and lo mein return the word chinese, and japchae and naengmyeon return the word korean. If the dish is not in the recognized list, return the phrase fusion cuisine. Examples: noodle("pho") returns "vietnamese", noodle("udon") returns "japanese".

title: Choral Voice Range
spec: Write a vocal classification tool `voice(part)` that describes the standard range for a given choir section. Soprano returns the phrase highest female voice, alto returns the phrase lowest female voice, and tenor returns the phrase highest male voice. Baritone returns the phrase middle male voice, bass returns the phrase lowest male voice, treble returns the phrase unchanged child voice, and countertenor returns the phrase falsetto male voice. For any unknown part, return the phrase undefined range. Examples: voice("soprano") returns "highest female voice", voice("bass") returns "lowest male voice".

title: Stage Lighting Gel
spec: Create a theatrical script with `color(mood)` that suggests a stage lighting gel color based on the desired emotional mood. A romantic or passionate mood suggests a red gel, a cold or isolated mood suggests a blue gel, and a natural or forest mood suggests a green gel. A sunny or happy mood suggests a yellow gel, a magical or mysterious mood suggests a purple gel, an alarming or dangerous mood suggests an amber gel, and a ghostly or supernatural mood suggests a cyan gel. Any other mood returns a clear gel. Examples: color("magical") returns "purple gel", color("cold") returns "blue gel".

title: Night Sky Hemisphere
spec: Design an astronomy helper `sky(star)` that tells the user which hemisphere a famous star or constellation is primarily visible from. Polaris, cassiopeia, and the big dipper return the northern hemisphere, while the southern cross, alpha centauri, and the magellanic clouds return the southern hemisphere. Orion, sirius, and the pleiades return the equatorial region. Include a helper that checks if a star's region is the equatorial region and returns the phrase visible globally, otherwise it returns the phrase restricted visibility. For unknown objects, return the phrase deep space. Examples: sky("polaris") returns "northern hemisphere", sky("orion") returns "equatorial region".

title: Airport Terminal Locator
spec: Implement a travel assistant `gate(airline)` that routes airline passengers to the correct airport terminal based on their carrier. Delta and air france depart from terminal one, united and lufthansa depart from terminal two, and american airlines and british airways depart from terminal three. Southwest and jetblue depart from terminal four, alaska airlines and hawaiian airlines depart from terminal five, and spirit and frontier depart from terminal six. Any other unlisted airline should return the international terminal. Examples: gate("delta") returns "terminal one", gate("spirit") returns "terminal six".

title: Dessert Flavor Profile
spec: Write a pastry chef tool `flavor(dessert)` that categorizes the dominant taste profile of a sweet treat. Lemon tart, key lime pie, and grapefruit sorbet map to the word citrus, while chocolate cake, brownies, and truffles map to the word rich. Strawberry shortcake, berry cobbler, and cherry pie map to the word fruity, and vanilla bean ice cream, panna cotta, and flan map to the word creamy. Peanut butter cookies, pecan pie, and almond biscotti map to the word nutty, and peppermint bark and mint chocolate chip map to the word minty. Any other dessert maps to the word sweet. Examples: flavor("lemon tart") returns "citrus", flavor("flan") returns "creamy".

title: Marine Depth Zone
spec: Create an oceanography module with `depth(organism)` that identifies the ocean layer where a specific sea creature typically lives. Phytoplankton, coral, and manatees return the epipelagic zone, while lanternfish, hatchetfish, and giant squid return the mesopelagic zone. Anglerfish, vampire squid, and gulper eels return the bathypelagic zone, and tripod fish, rattails, and sea pigs return the abyssopelagic zone. Snailfish and amphipods return the hadalpelagic zone. For any unidentified creature, return the phrase unknown depths. Examples: depth("coral") returns "epipelagic zone", depth("anglerfish") returns "bathypelagic zone".

title: Arena Ticket Tier
spec: Develop a ticketing system `tier(section)` that returns the price tier for a specific arena seating section. The floor, pit, and front row map to the phrase vip access, whereas the lower bowl, club level, and sideline map to the phrase premium seating. The upper bowl, mezzanine, and corner map to the phrase standard seating. The balcony, nosebleeds, and behind stage map to the phrase budget seating, and the standing room maps to the phrase general admission. Any other section returns the phrase invalid section. Examples: tier("pit") returns "vip access", tier("balcony") returns "budget seating".

title: Rocket Flight Stage
spec: Write an aerospace monitor `stage(altitude)` that returns the current phase of a rocket launch based on its altitude in kilometers. An altitude of exactly zero returns the phrase launch pad, one to ten returns the phrase max q phase, and eleven to fifty returns the phrase upper atmosphere. Fifty one to one hundred returns the phrase karman line approach, one hundred one to four hundred returns the phrase low earth orbit, and four hundred one to thirty five thousand returns the phrase medium earth orbit. Anything higher returns the phrase deep space transit, and if the altitude is negative, return the phrase telemetry error. Examples: stage(5) returns "max q phase", stage(200) returns "low earth orbit".

title: Volcano Tectonic Plate
spec: Implement a geological function `plate(volcano)` that associates famous volcanoes with their primary tectonic plate. Mount saint helens, mount rainier, and mount shasta return the north american plate, while mount fuji, krakatoa, and mount pinatubo return the eurasian plate. Mauna loa and kilauea return the pacific plate, mount kilimanjaro and erta ale return the african plate, mount vesuvius and mount etna return the african plate collision zone, and mount erebus returns the antarctic plate. If the volcano is unlisted, return the phrase unknown plate boundary. Examples: plate("mauna loa") returns "pacific plate", plate("mount fuji") returns "eurasian plate".

title: Speleothem Formation Type
spec: Create a cave exploration guide `cave(feature)` that categorizes mineral deposits found in caverns based on simple structural keywords. The keyword ceiling returns the word stalactites, the keyword floor returns the word stalagmites, and the keyword connected returns the word pillars. The keyword wall returns the word flowstones, the keyword tube returns the word soda straws, the keyword round returns the word cave pearls, and the keyword underwater returns the word pool fingers. Unidentified keywords return the phrase generic speleothem. Examples: cave("ceiling") returns "stalactites", cave("tube") returns "soda straws".

title: Fireworks Shell Type Identifier
spec: Write a program to identify aerial fireworks shells based on their visual effect descriptions. The main function `classify(effect)` evaluates a short text describing the explosion and returns the classic shell name. Return Peony for a spherical break without trails, Chrysanthemum for a spherical break with glowing trails, Willow for slowly falling lingering trails, or Crossette for stars splitting into pieces. Return Ring for a hollow circle shape, Kamuro for dense cascading crowns, Salute for a loud report with no color, and Palm for thick intersecting tendrils.

title: Pizza Style Classifier
spec: Create a module to determine regional pizza styles based on crust and baking characteristics. The entry function `evaluate(traits)` receives a list of descriptive words and returns the corresponding style. Return Neapolitan for wood fired leopard spotting, Chicago for deep dish cornmeal, New York for wide foldable slices, and Sicilian for a thick rectangular pan with airy dough. Output Detroit for a steel pan with crispy cheese edges, New Haven for coal fired char, St Louis for cracker thin crust with provel, and California for non traditional gourmet toppings.

title: Honey Floral Source Locator
spec: Develop a tool to categorize honey types based on color and tasting notes. Provide a function `analyze(profile)` that takes a text description of the honey and yields its floral source. Output Clover for a mild sweet light amber syrup, Orange Blossom for a pale color with citrus aromatics, Tupelo for a light golden hue that never crystallizes, or Manuka for a dark medicinal flavor. Return Buckwheat for a robust malty molasses taste, Acacia for a nearly clear liquid with vanilla hints, Wildflower for a variable multi floral blend, and Eucalyptus for medium amber with herbal menthol notes.

title: Bonsai Tree Style Namer
spec: Write a script to identify classical bonsai tree styling terms based on trunk angle and branch placement. Define a function `evaluate(features)` that takes a list of descriptive words and determines the Japanese term. Output Chokkan for a perfectly straight upright trunk, Moyogi for an upright trunk with gentle curves, Shakan for a slanted trunk, and Kengai for a cascading trunk falling below the pot base. Return Han kengai for a semi cascade reaching the rim, Fukinagashi for swept branches mimicking windswept trees, Bunjingi for a tall slender trunk with minimal foliage, and Yose ue for multiple separate trees planted together.

title: Heraldic Tincture Mapper
spec: Build a program that translates plain English color descriptions of coat of arms shields into traditional heraldic tincture terms. Create a function `translate(color)` that accepts a simple color word and maps it to the classic term. Return Gules if the input is red, Azure if the input is blue, Vert for green, and Purpure for purple. Output Sable for black, Or for gold or yellow, Argent for silver or white, and Tenne for orange or tawny. The function should default to Unknown if the input does not match any of these classic heraldic shades.

title: Whale Sound Categorizer
spec: Implement a system to classify cetacean vocalizations based on their acoustic properties. Write a function `classify(acoustic)` that processes a short text description of a recorded sound and identifies the call type. Yield Click for short broadband echolocation pulses, Whistle for continuous frequency modulated social calls, Moan for low frequency long duration sounds, and Song for complex repeating rhythmic sequences. Output Pulse for rapid burst calls used for close communication, Grunt for short low pitched aggressive noises, Trill for rapidly vibrating high pitched sounds, and Buzz for a rapid series of clicks during prey approach.

title: Fencing Parry Positioner
spec: Create a module to name classical fencing parries based on the blade line and hand position. The main function `identify(stance)` receives a text string detailing the defender posture and yields the numbered parry name. Output Prime for a high inside line with the thumb down, Seconde for a low outside line with a pronated hand, Tierce for a high outside line with a pronated wrist, and Quarte for a high inside line with a supinated hand. Return Quinte for protecting the head with a horizontal blade, Sixte for a high outside line with a supinated wrist, Septime for a low inside line with a supinated hand, and Octave for a low outside line with supination.

title: Ice Skating Jump Classifier
spec: Design a utility to name figure skating jumps based on their takeoff and landing edges. Define the entry function `judge(mechanics)` which takes a list of movement phrases and identifies the jump. Return Waltz for a forward outside edge takeoff with half rotation, Salchow for a backward inside edge takeoff, Toe Loop for a backward outside edge with a toe pick assist, and Loop for a backward outside edge takeoff without a toe pick. Output Flip for a backward inside edge with a toe pick, Lutz for a backward outside edge with a counter rotational toe pick, Axel for a forward outside edge takeoff with an extra half rotation, and Euler for landing on the backward inside edge of the opposite foot.

title: Ballet Movement Translator
spec: Write a program that translates physical descriptions of classical dance steps into formal ballet terminology. The function `translate(movement)` should evaluate a descriptive sentence and output the French term. Respond with Plie for bending the knees, Tendu for stretching the foot along the floor to a point, Jete for throwing the leg to leap, and Frappe for striking the floor with the ball of the foot. Return Fondue for a melting motion lowering on one bent leg, Grand Battement for a large forceful kick upward, Assemble for jumping off one foot and landing on two, and Pirouette for spinning on one leg.

title: Tap Dance Step Identifier
spec: Build a classifier for tap dance steps based on foot strikes and weight shifts. The entry function `analyze(sequence)` receives a text outline of dancer footwork and returns the step name. Return Shuffle for a forward brush followed immediately by a backward brush, Flap for a forward brush followed by a step with weight change, Ball Change for two quick steps alternating weight, and Cramp Roll for four rapid sounds stepping ball ball heel heel. Output Time Step for a rhythmic combination of shuffles and hops, Pullback for a backward hop brushing both feet, Wing for brushing the foot outward and inward while airborne, and Buffalo for a step shuffle leap combination traveling sideways.

title: Juggling Pattern Describer
spec: Create a tool to identify classic toss juggling patterns from trajectory descriptions. Provide a function `classify(trajectory)` that examines a sentence about how props are thrown and returns the pattern name. Yield Cascade for props crossing in a figure eight pattern, Fountain for props thrown and caught in the same hand without crossing, Shower for a circular pattern passing high and low, and Half Shower for a cascade with uneven throw heights. Return Mills Mess for crossing and uncrossing arms during a cascade, Rubenstein Revenge for complex arm crosses with flourishes, Box for synchronous vertical throws with horizontal passes, and Columns for props traveling straight up and down in parallel lines.

title: Typography Font Categorizer
spec: Develop a program to classify typeface designs based on letterform characteristics. The main function `categorize(features)` accepts a list of visual traits and outputs the typography category. Select Serif for small decorative lines at stroke ends, Sans Serif for clean lines without terminal flourishes, Slab Serif for thick block geometric terminators, and Script for connected cursive letterforms mimicking handwriting. Output Display for highly decorative shapes meant for large headings, Monospace for characters occupying the exact same horizontal width, Blackletter for thick and thin strokes resembling medieval calligraphy, and Decorative for novelty elements built into the letters.

title: Microscope Illumination Analyzer
spec: Write a script to identify microscopy lighting techniques from optical descriptions. Define a function `evaluate(optics)` that reads a short text string and determines the illumination method. Output Brightfield for a dark sample on a bright white background, Darkfield for illuminating from an angle to create a bright object on a black background, Phase Contrast for converting phase shifts into amplitude changes, and Fluorescence for using ultraviolet light to excite emitting compounds. Return Polarized for using cross oriented filters on birefringent materials, Confocal for using a spatial pinhole to eliminate out of focus light, DIC for using prisms to create pseudo three dimensional relief, and TIRF for lighting only a thin region near the boundary.

title: Metalworking Lathe Operation Namer
spec: Create a module that identifies machining operations on a center lathe based on tool movement and material removal. The function `identify(process)` receives a phrase describing the cutting action and yields the operation name. Return Facing for cutting across the end of a workpiece, Turning for moving the tool parallel to the axis to reduce diameter, Drilling for pushing a bit into the center axis, and Boring for enlarging an internal hole with a single point tool. Output Knurling for pressing a textured wheel into the surface for grip, Threading for cutting a helical groove along the cylinder, Parting for plunging a narrow blade to cut off a piece, and Grooving for cutting a narrow channel without severing.

title: Glassblowing Technique Classifier
spec: Build a classifier for hot glass manipulation methods based on the artisan actions. Write the entry function `classify(action)` that takes a text description and yields the technique name. Yield Gathering for dipping a pipe into the furnace to collect molten glass, Marvering for rolling hot glass on a flat steel table, Blowing for puffing air through the pipe to create a bubble, and Jacking for using metal blades to constrict the neckline. Return Puntying for attaching a solid iron rod to the base, Flaring for spinning the piece rapidly to open the lip, Optic for pressing the hot glass into a ribbed mold, and Frit for rolling the hot bubble in crushed colored glass chips.

title: Leatherworking Tool Identifier
spec: Develop a program to select the correct leather crafting tool based on the required task. Provide a function `select(task)` that evaluates a descriptive phrase and recommends the appropriate implement. Respond with Awl for piercing small holes for hand stitching, Skiver for thinning the edges of the hide, Edge Beveler for rounding off sharp square corners, and Burnisher for rubbing edges rapidly to create a glossy seal. Output Mallet for striking stamps or punches without damage, Groover for cutting a shallow trench to recess sewing threads, Creaser for pressing a decorative line parallel to the edge, and Punch for cutting out perfect circular holes for hardware.

title: Basket Weaving Pattern Namer
spec: Write a script to name traditional basketry weaving techniques from their structural descriptions. The main function `name(structure)` takes a short sentence and outputs the pattern name. Output Randings for weaving a single element alternately in front of and behind consecutive stakes, Pairing for twisting two weaving elements around each other between stakes, Waling for using three or more weavers twisted together to create a raised band, and Slewing for weaving two or more elements together as a single unit. Return Twining for wrapping elements tightly around warp threads, Plaiting for weaving flat uniform strips at right angles, Coiling for wrapping a core material sequentially and stitching it, and Ribbing for weaving back and forth across a fixed skeletal frame.

title: Printmaking Method Classifier
spec: Create a tool to categorize fine art printmaking techniques based on plate preparation and ink transfer. Define `categorize(prep)` to evaluate a descriptive text and return the medium. Return Etching for using acid to bite lines into a metal plate, Engraving for physically gouging lines into metal with a burin, Drypoint for scratching directly into a plate to create a fuzzy burr, and Mezzotint for rocking a plate to create millions of tiny dots. Output Aquatint for melting rosin dust onto a plate for textured washes, Lithography for drawing on a limestone block with a greasy crayon, Screenprint for forcing ink through a porous mesh stencil, and Woodcut for carving away negative space on a block.

title: Theater Stage Direction Locator
spec: Build a module to map descriptive actor movements to standard theatrical stage directions from the perspective of an actor facing the audience. The function `locate(movement)` receives a text string describing where the actor goes and returns the designated area. Output Downstage Center for moving directly forward toward the audience, Downstage Right for moving forward and right, Downstage Left for moving forward and left, and Center Stage for remaining in the exact middle. Return Center Stage Right for moving straight right from the middle, Center Stage Left for moving straight left from the middle, Upstage Center for moving directly backward away from the audience, and Upstage Right for moving backward and right.

title: Camera Shot Size Mapper
spec: Develop a program to translate visual framing descriptions into standard film production shot sizes. Write a function `frame(description)` that accepts a text phrase and selects the correct camera shot. Yield Extreme Wide for a tiny subject barely visible within a vast landscape, Wide for showing the subject entire body from head to toe, Full for framing tightly from the top of the head to the bottom of the feet, and Medium Wide for cutting the subject off around the knees. Return Medium for framing from the waist up, Medium Close for framing from the chest up, Close Up for showing only the face and shoulders, and Extreme Close for isolating a single detail like just the eyes.

title: Radio Frequency Band Categorizer
spec: Write a script to classify radio communications based on their electromagnetic spectrum usage and primary applications. The entry function `classify(application)` receives a descriptive sentence and outputs the band name. Return Extremely Low Frequency for submarine communication penetrating deep ocean water, Very Low Frequency for radio navigation and time signals, Low Frequency for long wave amplitude modulation broadcasting, and Medium Frequency for standard commercial amplitude modulation radio broadcasts. Output High Frequency for shortwave broadcasts bouncing off the ionosphere, Very High Frequency for frequency modulation radio and early analog television channels, Ultra High Frequency for digital television and cellular phones, and Super High Frequency for satellite communication and radar applications.

title: Computer Network Topology Identifier
spec: Create a utility to identify logical network layouts from connection descriptions. Define the function `identify(layout)` to read a text string and return the topology. Select Bus for all nodes connecting to a single central cable, Star for every node connecting individually to a central switch, Ring for nodes connecting in a closed loop, and Mesh for every node having a direct connection to every other node. Output Tree for a hierarchical structure with root nodes branching out to child nodes, Point to Point for a simple dedicated link connecting exactly two endpoints, Hybrid for combining two or more distinct architectural structures, and Daisy Chain for nodes linked sequentially one after another in a linear line.

title: Cell Organelle Function Mapper
spec: Build a biological classifier that maps cellular activities to the correct organelle. Provide a function `map(activity)` that takes a text phrase describing a biological process and returns the organelle name. Output Nucleus for storing genetic material and coordinating cellular replication, Mitochondria for generating chemical energy as adenosine triphosphate, Ribosome for translating messenger ribonucleic acid into polypeptide chains, and Endoplasmic Reticulum for folding and transporting synthesized proteins. Return Golgi Apparatus for modifying sorting and packaging proteins for secretion, Lysosome for breaking down waste materials with digestive enzymes, Vacuole for storing water nutrients and waste products in plant cells, and Chloroplast for converting light energy into sugars through photosynthesis.
